- `inReal` ({@struct/Record Record} array / numeric array, required): K-line (candlestick) data.
- `period` (number, optional): Calculation period.
- `multiplier` (number, optional): Multiplier (standard deviation multiplier).

Returns (array): The return value of the ```TA.BOLL()``` function is a two-dimensional array, with the structure ```[upLine, midLine, downLine]```.

Compute 20-period Bollinger Bands with 2 standard deviations once there are enough K-lines.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (records && records.length > 20) {
        var boll = TA.BOLL(records, 20, 2)
        var upLine = boll[0]
        var midLine = boll[1]
        var downLine = boll[2]
        Log(upLine)
        Log(midLine)
        Log(downLine)
        // Output: three arrays (upper, middle, lower band), each as long as the K-lines
    }
}
```

```python
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if records and len(records) > 20:
        boll = TA.BOLL(records, 20, 2)
        upLine = boll[0]
        midLine = boll[1]
        downLine = boll[2]
        Log(upLine)
        Log(midLine)
        Log(downLine)
        # Output: three arrays (upper, middle, lower band), each as long as the K-lines
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let Ok(records) = exchange.GetRecords(None, None, None) else { return };
    if records.len() > 20 {
        let boll = TA.BOLL(&records, 20, 2.0);
        let [upLine, midLine, downLine] = boll;
        Log!(upLine);
        Log!(midLine);
        Log!(downLine);
        // Output: three arrays (upper, middle, lower band), each as long as the K-lines
    }
}
```

The default values of the ```period``` and ```multiplier``` parameters of the ```TA.BOLL()``` function are ```20``` and ```2```, respectively.

See also: `TA`, `TA.MA`, `TA.ATR`, `TA.Highest`, `TA.Lowest`, `talib.BBANDS`

```javascript
    Log("lipsLine:", alligator[2])
    // Output: three arrays that are 8, 5 and 3 elements longer than the K-lines (padded with NaN at
    // the start)
}
```


#### TA.Highest

```
TA.Highest(inReal, period)
TA.Highest(inReal, period, attr)
```

The ```TA.Highest()``` function is used to calculate the **highest price within a period**.

Parameters:

- `inReal` ({@struct/Record Record} array / numeric array, required): K-line data or a numeric array.
- `period` (number, required): Period; required. ```0``` means all ```Bar```.
- `attr` (string, optional): Attribute. Optional values: ```Open```, ```Close```, ```Low```, ```High```, ```Volume```, ```OpenInterest```. When it is not passed, ```inReal``` is treated as a numeric array.

Returns (number): Maximum value of a certain attribute over the most recent specified period, not including the current Bar.

Compute the highest open price of the last 10 K-lines (excluding the current Bar).

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    var highestForOpen = TA.Highest(records, 10, "Open")
    Log(highestForOpen)
    // Output: a number: the highest open price of those 10 K-lines
}
```

```python
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    highestForOpen = TA.Highest(records, 10, "Open")
    Log(highestForOpen)
    # Output: a number: the highest open price of those 10 K-lines
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let Ok(records) = exchange.GetRecords(None, None, None) else { return };
    // Rust's TA.Highest has no attribute-name parameter; extract the open prices first
    let opens: Vec<f64> = records.iter().map(|r| r.Open).collect();
    let highestForOpen = TA.Highest(&opens, 10);
    Log!(highestForOpen);
    // Output: a number: the highest open price of those 10 K-lines
}
```

For example, ```TA.Highest(records, 30, "High")``` returns the highest ```High``` of the 30 bars before the current Bar. When ```period``` is ```0```, all ```Bar``` before the current one in ```inReal``` are used; when ```attr``` is not passed, ```inReal``` is treated as an ordinary numeric array.

When ```inReal``` has fewer than 2 elements, ```NaN``` is returned (```None``` in ```Python```).

In ```Rust```, ```TA.Highest(src, n)``` takes a numeric sequence (K-line data uses the close price); to calculate by field, use ```TA.HighestBy(&records, n, "High")```.

See also: `TA`, `TA.Lowest`, `TA.BOLL`, `TA.ATR`, `talib.MAX`

```python
    lowestForOpen = TA.Lowest(records, 10, "Open")
    Log(lowestForOpen)
    # Output: a number: the lowest open price of those 10 K-lines
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let Ok(records) = exchange.GetRecords(None, None, None) else { return };
    // Rust's TA.Lowest has no attribute-name parameter; extract the open prices first
    let opens: Vec<f64> = records.iter().map(|r| r.Open).collect();
    let lowestForOpen = TA.Lowest(&opens, 10);
    Log!(lowestForOpen);
    // Output: a number: the lowest open price of those 10 K-lines
}
```

For example, ```TA.Lowest(records, 30, "Low")``` returns the lowest ```Low``` of the 30 bars before the current Bar. When ```period``` is ```0```, all ```Bar``` before the current one in ```inReal``` are used; when ```attr``` is not passed, ```inReal``` is treated as an ordinary numeric array.

When ```inReal``` has fewer than 2 elements, ```NaN``` is returned (```None``` in ```Python```).

In ```Rust```, ```TA.Lowest(src, n)``` takes a numeric sequence (K-line data uses the close price); to calculate by field, use ```TA.LowestBy(&records, n, "Low")```.

See also: `TA`, `TA.Highest`, `TA.BOLL`, `TA.ATR`, `talib.MIN`

#### TA.SMA

```
TA.SMA(inReal)
TA.SMA(inReal, optInTimePeriod)
```

The ```TA.SMA()``` function is used to calculate the **Simple Moving Average (SMA) indicator**.

Parameters:

- `inReal` ({@struct/Record Record} array / numeric array, required): K-line (candlestick) data.
- `optInTimePeriod` (number, optional): Calculation period.

Returns (array): The return value of the ```TA.SMA()``` function is: a one-dimensional array.

Compute a 14-period SMA on 30-minute K-lines.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords(PERIOD_M30)
    if (!records) return
    var sma = TA.SMA(records, 14)
    Log(sma)
    // Output: an array as long as the K-lines; the warm-up part at the start is NaN
}
```

```python
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords(PERIOD_M30)
    if not records:
        return
    sma = TA.SMA(records, 14)
    Log(sma)
    # Output: a list as long as the K-lines; the warm-up part at the start is None
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let Ok(records) = exchange.GetRecords(None, PERIOD_M30, None) else { return };
    let sma = TA.SMA(&records, 14);
    Log!(sma);
    // Output: an array as long as the K-lines; the warm-up part at the start is NaN
}
```

The default value of the ```optInTimePeriod``` parameter of the ```TA.SMA()``` function is: ```9```.

```TA.SMA()``` is identical to ```TA.MA()```: both compute the simple moving average.

See also: `TA`, `TA.MA`, `TA.EMA`, `TA.RSI`, `talib.SMA`

### Talib

`talib` exposes the TA-Lib indicator library to `JavaScript` and `Python` strategies (not available in `Rust`).

In `JavaScript`, pass a K-line array (the fields each function needs are taken automatically) or numeric arrays. Functions with several outputs return a two-dimensional array, and the leading part with too few bars to compute is `NaN`.

In `Python`, `talib` is the TA-Lib Python package installed on the docker's machine (`pip install TA-Lib`, which depends on `numpy`); without it, any call raises `Please install talib module for python`. Pass numpy arrays such as `records.Close` as each function requires. Functions with several outputs return a `tuple` of numpy arrays. Functions that need several price fields (parameters named `inPriceHLC`, `inPriceOHLC` and so on) take each field as a separate array in order, for example `talib.ATR(records.High, records.Low, records.Close)`.

#### Moving average types (MAType)

Values of `optInMAType`, `optInFastMAType` and the other moving average type parameters; all default to `0` (SMA).

| Value | Moving average type |
| - | - |
| `0` | SMA (Simple Moving Average) |
| `1` | EMA (Exponential Moving Average) |
| `2` | WMA (Weighted Moving Average) |
| `3` | DEMA (Double Exponential Moving Average) |
| `4` | TEMA (Triple Exponential Moving Average) |
| `5` | TRIMA (Triangular Moving Average) |
| `6` | KAMA (Kaufman Adaptive Moving Average) |
| `7` | MAMA (MESA Adaptive Moving Average) |
| `8` | T3 (T3 Triple Exponential Moving Average) |

#### Overlap Studies

Overlap studies are plotted on the same scale as price: moving averages, Bollinger Bands, parabolic SAR and similar.

##### talib.ACCBANDS

```
talib.ACCBANDS(inPriceHLC)
talib.ACCBANDS(inPriceHLC, optInTimePeriod)
```

Calculates the Acceleration Bands and returns the upper band, middle band and lower band.

Parameters:

- `inPriceHLC` ({@struct/Record Record} array, required): K-line array; the high, low and close fields are used. In Python, pass `records.High`, `records.Low`, `records.Close` in this order.
- `optInTimePeriod` (number, optional): Calculation period. Default `20`.

Returns (array): Two-dimensional array: [upper band array, middle band array, lower band array] (a tuple in the same order in Python).

Compute the Acceleration Bands from the latest K-lines.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    var ret = talib.ACCBANDS(records)
    // Output: [upper band array, middle band array, lower band array]
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    upper, middle, lower = talib.ACCBANDS(records.High, records.Low, records.Close)
    # Output: (upper band array, middle band array, lower band array)
    Log(upper, middle, lower)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `ACCBANDS(Records[High,Low,Close],Time Period = 20) = [Array(outRealUpperBand),Array(outRealMiddleBand),Array(outRealLowerBand)]`.

The upper band is the simple moving average of `High * (1 + 4 * (High - Low) / (High + Low))`, the middle band is the simple moving average of the close price, and the lower band is the simple moving average of `Low * (1 - 4 * (High - Low) / (High + Low))`, all over `optInTimePeriod` bars.

In `Python`, TA-Lib provides this function from version 0.6 (both the C library and the Python package must be 0.6 or later); older versions raise an attribute error.

See also: `talib.BBANDS`, `talib.SMA`, `talib.ATR`, `TA.BOLL`

##### talib.MAVP

```
talib.MAVP(inReal, inPeriods)
talib.MAVP(inReal, inPeriods, optInMinPeriod)
talib.MAVP(inReal, inPeriods, optInMinPeriod, optInMaxPeriod)
talib.MAVP(inReal, inPeriods, optInMinPeriod, optInMaxPeriod, optInMAType)
```

Calculates the Moving Average with Variable Period.

Parameters:

- `inReal` (numeric array, required): Series to average.
- `inPeriods` (numeric array, required): Period used for each bar; it must have the same length as `inReal`. Values outside `[optInMinPeriod, optInMaxPeriod]` are clamped to the bounds.
- `optInMinPeriod` (number, optional): Minimum period. Default `2`.
- `optInMaxPeriod` (number, optional): Maximum period. Default `30`.
- `optInMAType` (number, optional): Moving average type; see the MAType table on the `Talib` page. Default `0` (SMA).

Returns (numeric array): Indicator values, the same length as the input; the leading values without enough data are `NaN`.

Compute a variable-period average using 10 for up bars and 20 for down bars.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    var closes = records.map(function(r) { return r.Close })
    // period per bar: 10 for up bars, 20 for down bars (for illustration only)
    var periods = records.map(function(r) { return r.Close > r.Open ? 10 : 20 })
    var ret = talib.MAVP(closes, periods, 10, 20)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
import numpy as np
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    # period per bar: 10 for up bars, 20 for down bars (for illustration only)
    periods = np.array([10.0 if r["Close"] > r["Open"] else 20.0 for r in records])
    ret = talib.MAVP(records.Close, periods, 10, 20)
    Log(ret)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `MAVP(Array(inReal),Array(inPeriods),Min Period = 2,Max Period = 30,MA Type = 0) = Array(outReal)`.

The `i`-th value is the moving average of `inReal` up to element `i` with period `inPeriods[i]`; the first `optInMaxPeriod - 1` values are `NaN` (regardless of the actual values in `inPeriods`).

Both inputs must be numeric arrays: in `JavaScript`, extract a field from the K-line data with `map` first; if a K-line array is passed, both inputs take the close price of the same K-line data and the result is meaningless; arrays of different lengths raise an error. In `Python`, both inputs must be numpy arrays of type `float64`.

See also: `talib.MA`, `talib.SMA`, `talib.EMA`, `TA.MA`

Calculates the Triple Exponential Moving Average (T3).

Parameters:

- `inReal` ({@struct/Record Record} array / numeric array, required): K-line array (close prices are used) or numeric array; in Python, pass a numeric array such as `records.Close`.
- `optInTimePeriod` (number, optional): Calculation period. Default `5`.
- `optInVFactor` (number, optional): Smoothing factor (Volume Factor), between `0` and `1`. Default `0.7`.

Returns (numeric array): Indicator values, the same length as the input; the leading values without enough data are `NaN`.

Compute the Triple Exponential Moving Average (T3) from the latest K-lines.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    var ret = talib.T3(records)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
    if not records:

    ret = talib.T3(records.Close)

```

In `Python`, TA-Lib provides this function from version 0.6 (both the C library and the Python package must be 0.6 or later); older versions raise an attribute error.

Parameters:

- `inReal` ({@struct/Record Record} array / numeric array, required): K-line array (close prices are used) or numeric array; in Python, pass a numeric array such as `records.Close`.
- `optInTimePeriod` (number, optional): Calculation period. Default `14`.

Returns (numeric array): Indicator values, the same length as the input; the leading values without enough data are `NaN`.



Each value is the mean of the absolute differences between the last `optInTimePeriod` values and their average.

In `Python`, TA-Lib provides this function from version 0.6 (both the C library and the Python package must be 0.6 or later); older versions raise an attribute error.

#### Statistic Functions

Statistic functions compute statistics over a sliding window: beta, Pearson's correlation coefficient, linear regression, standard deviation, variance and time series forecast.

##### talib.BETA

```
talib.BETA(inReal0, inReal1)
talib.BETA(inReal0, inReal1, optInTimePeriod)
```

Calculates the Beta.

Parameters:

- `inReal0` (numeric array, required): First price series (the benchmark).
- `inReal1` (numeric array, required): Second price series; it must have the same length as `inReal0`.
- `optInTimePeriod` (number, optional): Calculation period. Default `5`.

Returns (numeric array): Indicator values, the same length as the input; the leading values without enough data are `NaN`.

Compute the beta of the second exchange's symbol against the first one (the benchmark).

```javascript
function main() {
    // exchanges[0] is the benchmark, exchanges[1] is the instrument whose beta is calculated
    var r0 = exchanges[0].GetRecords()
    var r1 = exchanges[1].GetRecords()
    if (!r0 || !r1) return
    var n = Math.min(r0.length, r1.length)
    var c0 = r0.slice(-n).map(function(r) { return r.Close })
    var c1 = r1.slice(-n).map(function(r) { return r.Close })
    var ret = talib.BETA(c0, c1, 5)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
def main():
    # exchanges[0] is the benchmark, exchanges[1] is the instrument whose beta is calculated
    r0 = exchanges[0].GetRecords()
    r1 = exchanges[1].GetRecords()
    if not r0 or not r1:
        return
    n = min(len(r0), len(r1))
    ret = talib.BETA(r0.Close[-n:], r1.Close[-n:], 5)
    Log(ret)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `BETA(Array(inReal0),Array(inReal1),Time Period = 5) = Array(outReal)`.

Takes the bar-by-bar rate of change of `inReal0` as the independent variable and that of `inReal1` as the dependent variable, runs a linear regression over the latest `optInTimePeriod` changes and returns the slope. To get the beta of an instrument against a benchmark, pass the benchmark prices as `inReal0` and the instrument prices as `inReal1`.

In `JavaScript`, both inputs must be numeric arrays (extract a field from the K-line data with `map` first): if a K-line array is passed, both inputs take the close price of the same K-line data and the result is meaningless; arrays of different lengths raise an error.

See also: `talib.CORREL`, `talib.LINEARREG_SLOPE`, `talib.VAR`

##### talib.CORREL

```
talib.CORREL(inReal0, inReal1)
talib.CORREL(inReal0, inReal1, optInTimePeriod)
```

Calculates the Pearson's Correlation Coefficient (r).

Parameters:

- `inReal0` (numeric array, required): First series.
- `inReal1` (numeric array, required): Second series; it must have the same length as `inReal0`.
- `optInTimePeriod` (number, optional): Calculation period. Default `30`.

Returns (numeric array): Indicator values, the same length as the input; the leading values without enough data are `NaN`.

Compute the correlation between close price and volume over 30 K-lines.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    var closes = records.map(function(r) { return r.Close })
    var volumes = records.map(function(r) { return r.Volume })
    var ret = talib.CORREL(closes, volumes, 30)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    ret = talib.CORREL(records.Close, records.Volume, 30)
    Log(ret)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `CORREL(Array(inReal0),Array(inReal1),Time Period = 30) = Array(outReal)`.

Returns Pearson's correlation coefficient of the two series over the latest `optInTimePeriod` bars, in the range [-1, 1].

In `JavaScript`, both inputs must be numeric arrays (extract a field from the K-line data with `map` first): if a K-line array is passed, both inputs take the close price of the same K-line data and the result is meaningless; arrays of different lengths raise an error.

See also: `talib.BETA`, `talib.LINEARREG`, `talib.STDDEV`

#### Math Operators

Math operators cover element-wise addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of two arrays, plus the maximum, minimum, their indexes and the sum over a period.

##### talib.ADD

```
talib.ADD(inReal0, inReal1)
```

Adds two arrays element by element (Vector Arithmetic Add).

Parameters:

- `inReal0` (numeric array, required): First series.
- `inReal1` (numeric array, required): Second series; it must have the same length as `inReal0`.

Returns (numeric array): Results, the same length as the input.

Add the high and low price of each K-line.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    // high price plus low price
    var highs = records.map(function(r) { return r.High })
    var lows = records.map(function(r) { return r.Low })
    var ret = talib.ADD(highs, lows)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    # high price plus low price
    ret = talib.ADD(records.High, records.Low)
    Log(ret)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `ADD(Array(inReal0),Array(inReal1)) = Array(outReal)`.

Calculates `inReal0[i] + inReal1[i]` element by element.

In `JavaScript`, both inputs must be numeric arrays (extract a field from the K-line data with `map` first): if a K-line array is passed, both inputs take the close price of the same K-line data and the result is meaningless; arrays of different lengths raise an error.

See also: `talib.SUB`, `talib.MULT`, `talib.DIV`

##### talib.DIV

```
talib.DIV(inReal0, inReal1)
```

Divides the first array by the second, element by element (Vector Arithmetic Div).

Parameters:

- `inReal0` (numeric array, required): First series.
- `inReal1` (numeric array, required): Second series; it must have the same length as `inReal0`.

Returns (numeric array): Results, the same length as the input.

Divide the close price of each K-line by its open price.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    // close price divided by open price
    var closes = records.map(function(r) { return r.Close })
    var opens = records.map(function(r) { return r.Open })
    var ret = talib.DIV(closes, opens)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    # close price divided by open price
    ret = talib.DIV(records.Close, records.Open)
    Log(ret)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `DIV(Array(inReal0),Array(inReal1)) = Array(outReal)`.

Calculates `inReal0[i] / inReal1[i]` element by element.

In `JavaScript`, both inputs must be numeric arrays (extract a field from the K-line data with `map` first): if a K-line array is passed, both inputs take the close price of the same K-line data and the result is meaningless; arrays of different lengths raise an error.

See also: `talib.MULT`, `talib.ADD`, `talib.SUB`


TA-Lib equivalent: `MINMAXINDEX(Records[Close],Time Period = 30) = [Array(outMinIdx),Array(outMaxIdx)]`.

See also: `talib.MININDEX`, `talib.MAXINDEX`, `talib.MINMAX`

##### talib.MULT

```
talib.MULT(inReal0, inReal1)
```

Multiplies two arrays element by element (Vector Arithmetic Mult).

Parameters:

- `inReal0` (numeric array, required): First series.
- `inReal1` (numeric array, required): Second series; it must have the same length as `inReal0`.

Returns (numeric array): Results, the same length as the input.

Multiply the close price of each K-line by its volume.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    // close price multiplied by volume
    var closes = records.map(function(r) { return r.Close })
    var volumes = records.map(function(r) { return r.Volume })
    var ret = talib.MULT(closes, volumes)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    # close price multiplied by volume
    ret = talib.MULT(records.Close, records.Volume)
    Log(ret)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `MULT(Array(inReal0),Array(inReal1)) = Array(outReal)`.

Calculates `inReal0[i] * inReal1[i]` element by element.

In `JavaScript`, both inputs must be numeric arrays (extract a field from the K-line data with `map` first): if a K-line array is passed, both inputs take the close price of the same K-line data and the result is meaningless; arrays of different lengths raise an error.

See also: `talib.DIV`, `talib.ADD`, `talib.SUB`

##### talib.SUB

```
talib.SUB(inReal0, inReal1)
```

Subtracts the second array from the first, element by element (Vector Arithmetic Subtraction).

Parameters:

- `inReal0` (numeric array, required): First series.
- `inReal1` (numeric array, required): Second series; it must have the same length as `inReal0`.

Returns (numeric array): Results, the same length as the input.

Subtract the low price from the high price of each K-line.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    // high price minus low price
    var highs = records.map(function(r) { return r.High })
    var lows = records.map(function(r) { return r.Low })
    var ret = talib.SUB(highs, lows)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    # high price minus low price
    ret = talib.SUB(records.High, records.Low)
    Log(ret)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `SUB(Array(inReal0),Array(inReal1)) = Array(outReal)`.

Calculates `inReal0[i] - inReal1[i]` element by element.

In `JavaScript`, both inputs must be numeric arrays (extract a field from the K-line data with `map` first): if a K-line array is passed, both inputs take the close price of the same K-line data and the result is meaningless; arrays of different lengths raise an error.

See also: `talib.ADD`, `talib.MULT`, `talib.DIV`

##### talib.SUM

```
talib.SUM(inReal)
talib.SUM(inReal, optInTimePeriod)
```

Calculates the Summation.

Parameters:

- `inReal` ({@struct/Record Record} array / numeric array, required): K-line array (close prices are used) or numeric array; in Python, pass a numeric array such as `records.Close`.
- `optInTimePeriod` (number, optional): Calculation period. Default `30`.

Returns (numeric array): Indicator values, the same length as the input; the leading values without enough data are `NaN`.

Compute the Summation from the latest K-lines.

```javascript
function main() {
    var records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if (!records) return
    var ret = talib.SUM(records)
    Log(ret)
}
```

```python
import talib
def main():
    records = exchange.GetRecords()
    if not records:
        return
    ret = talib.SUM(records.Close)
    Log(ret)
```

TA-Lib equivalent: `SUM(Records[Close],Time Period = 30) = Array(outReal)`.

See also: `talib.ADD`, `talib.SMA`, `talib.MAX`

#### Pattern Recognition

Pattern recognition functions detect classic candlestick patterns: a non-zero value where the pattern appears (positive for bullish, negative for bearish, usually `100` or `-100`), otherwise `0`. In JavaScript, the leading part with too few bars to compute is `NaN`.

### OS

FMZ Quant Trading Platform supports file read/write operations. The os library provides a complete file system operation interface to help users with data persistence, configuration management, and logging during strategy development.
Note that this feature only supports ```JavaScript``` language strategies.

The os library supports: File objects, File list objects, and File information objects.
| Object | Description | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| File Object: File | Provides file read/write, positioning and other operations. | Obtained through ```os.open()```, need to call ```close()``` to release resources after use. |
| File List Object: ListFilesResult | Used to record directory listing information. | Supports wildcard matching patterns, returned by ```os.listFiles()``` function. |
| File Information Object: FileStat | File statistics information. | Returned by ```os.stat()``` function. |

Supports live trading and backtesting systems.
- Live trading environment:
  Each live trading has its own file directory: the ```files``` folder at the same level as the live trading database file in the docker directory, i.e. ```logs/storage/xxx/files``` (relative to the docker directory), where ```xxx``` is the live trading ID, and the docker program (robot) is at the same level as ```logs```. Files of different live tradings do not affect each other.
- Backtesting system environment:
  The backtesting system is a sandbox environment. The system simulates a file directory with the default directory: ```/logs/storage/1/files```.
  When backtesting ends, the created file contents will be cleared.

#### os

The os library provides a complete file system operation interface for the FMZ Quant Trading Platform.

##### os.open

```
open(filename)
open(filename, mode)
```

Open a file in the specified mode.

Parameters:

- `filename` (string, required): File name. The parameter ```filename``` is a path containing the file name. Since both the docker and backtesting system support ```os``` operations, please note that in **non-backtesting environments**, file operations are restricted to the ```files``` folder at the same level as the live trading database file in the docker directory, therefore absolute paths are not supported for operating any files (a leading ```/``` is ignored, and the path must not contain ```..```). The path parameters of the other ```os``` functions follow the same restriction, see `OS`.
- `mode` (string, optional): Specify the file opening mode.

Returns (`File` object): ```File``` object for file operations. If opening fails (e.g. the file does not exist in read-only mode, or the mode string is invalid), an exception is thrown.

Create a file, write data, then read it.

```javascript
function main() {
    let fileHandle = os.open("output.txt", "w+")
    let bytesWritten = fileHandle.write("Hello FMZ!")
    Log("Bytes written:", bytesWritten)
    // Output: Bytes written: 10
    fileHandle.seek(0, 0)
    let fileContent = fileHandle.read()
    Log("File content read:", fileContent)
    // Output: File content read: Hello FMZ!
    fileHandle.close()
}
```

File opening modes:

  - ```r``` : read (read-only, file must exist)

  - ```w``` : write (write-only, creates file if it doesn't exist, clears content if it exists)

  - ```a``` : append (append write, creates file if it doesn't exist, writes to the end if it exists)

  - ```+``` : Adding + after r/w/a means both read and write are allowed (e.g., "r+", "w+", "a+"); the file is created if it does not exist (also with "r+")

  - ```b``` : binary (binary mode, e.g., "rb", "rb+": ```read()``` returns an ```ArrayBuffer``` instead of a string)

Mode characters can be combined freely (e.g. "rb+", "wb"); any other character throws an exception.

Files are opened/created in the ```files``` folder under the live trading database file directory (xxx.db3, where xxx is the live trading Id). When a file is opened for writing (```w```, ```a```, ```+```), missing parent directories in the path are created automatically.

See also: `os`, `File`, `os.fgets`, `os.fputs`, `os.exists`

##### os.fgets

```
fgets(filename)
```

Read the entire file content at once.

Parameters:

- `filename` (string, required): File path, including the filename to be read.

Returns (string): Returns the complete content of the file.

Read the content of a configuration file.

```javascript
function main() {
    // create and write the file first
    // let fileHandle = os.open("config.json", "w+")
    // let objJson = {"name": "tom", "age": 18}
    // fileHandle.write(JSON.stringify(objJson))
    // fileHandle.close()

    let content = os.fgets("config.json")
    Log("Config content:", content)
    // Output: Config content: {"name":"tom","age":18}
}
```

Suitable for quick reading of small files, loading the entire file content into memory at once.

If the file does not exist, the ```fgets()``` function throws an exception.

See also: `os`, `os.open`, `os.fputs`, `os.mmap`

##### os.fputs

```
fputs(filename, content)
fputs(filename, content, append)
```

Write content to a file.

Parameters:

- `filename` (string, required): File path.
- `content` (string, required): Content to write.
- `append` (bool, optional): Whether to write in append mode, defaults to false (overwrite mode).

Returns (number): Returns the actual number of bytes written.

Save strategy configuration to file.

```javascript
function main() {
    let config = '{"strategy": "MA", "period": 20}'
    let bytesWritten = os.fputs("strategy_config.json", config)
    Log("Bytes written:", bytesWritten)
    // Output: Bytes written: 32
    Log(`os.fgets("strategy_config.json"):`, os.fgets("strategy_config.json"))
    // Output: os.fgets("strategy_config.json"): {"strategy": "MA", "period": 20}

    // append a log line
    let logInfo = "\n[" + new Date().toISOString() + "] Config saved"
    os.fputs("strategy_config.json", logInfo, true)
    Log(`os.fgets("strategy_config.json"):`, os.fgets("strategy_config.json"))
    // Output: os.fgets("strategy_config.json"): {"strategy": "MA", "period": 20}
    // [2025-09-08T07:20:30.563Z] Config saved
}
```

Convenient file writing method, overwrites file content by default. Set append to true to append to the end of the file.

See also: `os`, `os.fgets`, `os.open`

##### os.mmap

```
mmap(filename)
```

Reads the whole file and returns its binary data as an ArrayBuffer.

Parameters:

- `filename` (string, required): File path.

Returns (ArrayBuffer): Returns the binary data of the file content.

Map the binary data of a file.

```javascript
function ab2str(buf) {
    let arr = new Uint8Array(buf)
    return String.fromCharCode.apply(null, arr)
}

function main() {
    let buffer = os.mmap("strategyConfig/testData.txt")
    Log("File size in bytes:", buffer.byteLength)
    let arr = Array.from(new Uint8Array(buffer))
    Log("arr:",  arr)
    // Output: arr: [72,101,108,108,111,32,70,77,90,33]
    Log("ab2str(buffer):", ab2str(buffer))
    // Output: ab2str(buffer): Hello FMZ!
}
```

Reads the entire file into memory at once and returns it as an ArrayBuffer (it is not an on-demand memory mapping; a large file takes the same amount of memory).

See also: `os`, `os.fgets`, `os.open`

##### os.getRootDir

```
getRootDir()
```

Get the root directory path for file operations.

Returns (string): Returns the path of the root directory.

Get and display the root directory path.

```javascript
function main() {
    let rootDir = os.getRootDir()
    Log("Root directory:", rootDir)
}
```

See also: `os`, `os.listFiles`, `os.mkdir`

##### os.listFiles

```
listFiles()
listFiles(pattern)
```

List files and subdirectories in the specified directory.

Parameters:

- `pattern` (string, optional): Optional matching pattern, supports wildcards (e.g., *.txt, data_*.json), can specify directory path.

Returns (`ListFilesResult` object): A `ListFilesResult` object: ```files``` is the array of matching file names and ```dirs``` the array of subdirectories of the current directory.

List matched files and directories.

```javascript
function main() {
    // list all json files
    let result = os.listFiles("*.json")
    Log("result:", result)

    // list everything
    let allFiles = os.listFiles()
    Log("allFiles:", allFiles)
}
```

When the ```pattern``` parameter is not specified, lists all files and subdirectories in the file root directory (the directory returned by `getRootDir`). When ```pattern``` is a directory path, that directory is listed; wildcards (```*```, ```?```) are only allowed in the last path segment, e.g. ```data/*.json```, and the returned names then carry the directory prefix (e.g. ```data/a.json```).

See also: `os`, `ListFilesResult`, `os.getRootDir`, `os.stat`

##### os.exists

```
exists(filename)
```

Check if the specified file or directory exists.

Parameters:

- `filename` (string, required): The file or directory path to check.

Returns (bool): Returns true if the file or directory exists, otherwise returns false.

Check if a file or path exists.

```javascript
function main() {
    Log(`os.exists("./strategyConfig"):`, os.exists("./strategyConfig"))
    // Output: os.exists("./strategyConfig"): true
    Log(`os.exists("./strategyConfig/testData.txt"):`, os.exists("./strategyConfig/testData.txt"))
    // Output: os.exists("./strategyConfig/testData.txt"): true
    // Log(`os.exists("../strategyConfig"):`, os.exists("../strategyConfig"))   // a path containing
    // ".." throws: invalid path: path traversal not allowed
    Log(`os.exists("test_1.txt"):`, os.exists("test_1.txt"))
    // Output: os.exists("test_1.txt"): true
    Log(`os.exists("test_2.txt"):`, os.exists("test_2.txt"))
    // Output: os.exists("test_2.txt"): false
}
```

See also: `os`, `os.stat`, `os.open`

##### os.remove

```
remove(filename)
```

Delete the specified file or empty directory.

Parameters:

- `filename` (string, required): The file path to delete.

Returns (bool): Returns true on successful deletion; throws an exception on failure (can be caught with try...catch).

Example of deleting a file.

```javascript
function main() {
    let tempFile = "test_1.txt"
    if (os.exists(tempFile)) {
        let success = os.remove(tempFile)
        Log("Temp file deleted:", success)
    }
}
```

This function deletes a file or an empty directory. To delete a non-empty directory, use the ```rmdir()``` function.

See also: `os`, `os.exists`, `os.rmdir`, `os.rename`

##### os.mkdir

```
mkdir(dirname)
```

Create a directory.

Parameters:

- `dirname` (string, required): The directory path to create.

Returns (bool): Returns true if creation is successful; throws an exception on failure (can be caught with try...catch).

Create a data storage directory, create a file and write data.

```javascript
function main() {
    let success = os.mkdir("data/backtest/results")
    Log("Directory created:", success)

    if (success) {
        os.fputs("data/backtest/results/summary.txt", "Backtest completed")
    }
}
```

Supports recursive creation of multi-level directories. If parent directories do not exist, they will be created automatically.

See also: `os`, `os.rmdir`, `os.getRootDir`

##### os.rmdir

```
rmdir(dirname)
```

Remove a directory and all its contents.

Parameters:

- `dirname` (string, required): The directory path to be removed.

Returns (bool): Returns true on successful deletion; throws an exception on failure (can be caught with try...catch).

Remove a directory and all its contents.

```javascript
function main() {
    let tempDir = "data"
    if (os.exists(tempDir)) {
        let success = os.rmdir(tempDir)
        Log("directory removed:", success)
    }
}
```

This operation will permanently delete the directory and all its contents, please use with caution.

See also: `os`, `os.mkdir`, `os.remove`

##### os.rename

```
rename(oldName, newName)
```

Rename a file or move a file.

Parameters:

- `oldName` (string, required): The name or path of the original file.
- `newName` (string, required): The name or path of the new file.

Returns (bool): Returns true when the operation succeeds; throws an exception on failure (can be caught with try...catch).

Rename a file and move it to another directory.

```javascript
function main() {
    let oldFileName = "output.txt"
    let newFileName = "outputFiles/" + new Date().getTime() + "output.txt"
    // let retRename = os.rename(oldFileName, newFileName)
    // Log("retRename:", retRename)  // the target directory outputFiles does not exist, so rename
    // throws an exception

    os.mkdir("outputFiles")
    let retRename = os.rename(oldFileName, newFileName)
    Log("retRename:", retRename)
    // Output: retRename: true
}
```

This function can be used to rename a file or move a file to another directory. If the directory of the new path does not exist, the operation will fail.

See also: `os`, `os.remove`, `os.exists`

##### os.stat

```
stat(filename)
```

Get detailed statistics information of a file.

Parameters:

- `filename` (string, required): File path.

Returns (`FileStat` object): Returns an object containing file statistics information.

Get file information and check file size.

```javascript
function main() {
    if (os.exists("strategyConfig/testData.txt")) {
        let stat = os.stat("strategyConfig/testData.txt")
        Log("stat:", stat)
        // Output: stat: {"size":10,"mode":420,"mtime":1757312981796,"atime":1757312981796,"ctime":1757312981796}
    }
}
```

The returned ```FileStat``` object contains the following fields:

  - size: File size.

  - mode: File mode value; the low 9 bits are the permission bits (420 for a regular 0644 file), and directories and other special files carry extra type flag bits.

  - mtime: Last modification time, millisecond timestamp.

  - atime: Currently the same as mtime.

  - ctime: Currently the same as mtime.

See also: `os`, `FileStat`, `os.exists`

##### os.exit

```
exit()
exit(status)
```

Exit the program.

Parameters:

- `status` (number, optional): Optional exit status code, default value is 0.

Exit program after checking conditions.

```javascript
function main() {
    if (!os.exists("required_config.json")) {
        Log("Required configuration file not found!")
        os.exit(1)  // Abnormal exit
    }
    Log("Configuration found, continuing...")
    // Normal strategy logic...
}
```

Immediately terminates the strategy process without running ```onexit()``` or other cleanup functions. Status code 0 indicates a normal finish (the live trading is shown as completed), non-zero values indicate abnormal exit (the live trading is shown as error).

See also: `os`, `os.getRootDir`

#### File

File object that provides file read/write, positioning and other operations.

##### File.close

```
close()
```

Close the file and release associated resources.

Example of proper file operation workflow.

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("data.txt", "w")
    file.write("Hello FMZ!")
    file.close()  // the file must be closed
}
```

This method must be called after using the file object to release system resources.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.flush`

##### File.puts

```
puts(data1, data2, ...dataN)
```

Write one or more strings to a file.

Parameters:

- `data` (string, required): String data to be written, multiple parameters can be passed.

Returns (number): Returns the actual number of bytes written.

Write multiple strings to a file.

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("output.txt", "w+")
    let bytes = file.puts("Hello", " ", "World", "!")
    Log("Bytes written:", bytes)
    // Output: Bytes written: 12

    file.seek(0, 0)
    let data = file.read()
    Log("data:", data)
    // Output: data: Hello World!
    // If the file is opened with os.open("output.txt", "w") (write-only), read() throws

    // file.puts()                // error: puts requires at least 1 argument at main
    file.puts(", Hello FMZ!")

    file.seek(0, 0)
    data = file.read()
    Log("data:", data)
    // Output: data: Hello World!, Hello FMZ!
    file.close()
}
```

Multiple string parameters can be written at once, they will be concatenated in order and then written.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.printf`, `File.write`, `File.flush`

##### File.printf

```
printf(format)
printf(format, arg1, arg2, ...argN)
```

Write formatted data to file.

Parameters:

- `format` (string, required): Format string.
- `args` (any, optional): Format arguments.

Returns (number): Returns the actual number of bytes written.

Write formatted trading data.

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("trade_log.txt", "w+")
    let price = 100.25
    let volume = 1000
    let bytes = file.printf("Price: %.2f, Volume: %d\n", price, volume)
    Log("Formatted bytes written:", bytes)

    file.seek(0, 0)
    let data = file.read()
    Log("data:", data)
    // Output: data: Price: 100.25, Volume: 1000

    // file.printf("| Price: %.2f, Volume: %d\n")   // "| Price: %!f(MISSING), Volume: %!d(MISSING)"
    // file.seek(0, 0)
    // data = file.read()
    // Log("data:", data)

    file.close()
}
```

Supported verbs: ```%s```, ```%d```, ```%f```, ```%v``` and ```%%```, with flags (```-```, ```0```), width and precision, e.g. ```%.2f```, ```%-8s```, ```%08d```. A missing argument is written as placeholder text such as ```%!d(MISSING)```.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.puts`, `File.write`

##### File.flush

```
flush()
```

Flush the file buffer to ensure data is written to disk.

Write important log data in real-time.

```javascript
function main() {
    let logFile = os.open("critical.log", "a")
    logFile.printf("[%s] Critical event occurred\n", new Date().toISOString())   // [2025-09-09T03:15:43.895Z] Critical event occurred
    logFile.flush()  // Immediately write data to disk
    // Continue with other operations...
    logFile.close()
}
```

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.close`, `File.write`

##### File.tell

```
tell()
```

Get the current file pointer position.

Returns (number): Returns the current file pointer position (offset in bytes).

Track position during file operations.

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("data.txt", "r+")
    Log("Initial position:", file.tell())
    // Output: Initial position: 0

    file.write("Hello")
    Log("After write position:", file.tell())
    // Output: After write position: 5
    file.close()
}
```

Returns the byte offset of the current file pointer relative to the beginning of the file.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.seek`, `File.eof`

##### File.seek

```
seek(offset, whence)
```

Move the file pointer to a specified position.

Parameters:

- `offset` (number, required): Offset (in bytes).
- `whence` (number, required): Reference position: 0=beginning of file, 1=current position, 2=end of file.

Returns (number): Returns the new file pointer position.

Read characters in reverse order.

```javascript
function main() {
    let str = "Hello FMZ!"
    let file = os.open("data.txt", "w+")
    file.write(str)

    // If i > str.length, seek() throws an exception (invalid argument)
    for (let i = 1; i <= str.length; i++) {
        file.seek(-i, 2)
        let data = file.read(1)
        Log("i:", i, ", data:", data)
    }

    file.close()
}
```

Used to position the file pointer, the ```offset``` parameter can be negative (indicating backward movement).

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.tell`, `File.eof`

##### File.eof

```
eof()
```

Check if the file pointer has reached the end of file.

Returns (bool): Returns true if end of file has been reached, otherwise returns false.

Read file line by line until end of file.

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("data.txt", "r")
    let lineCount = 0

    while (!file.eof()) {
        let line = file.getline()
        if (line !== undefined) {
            lineCount++
            Log("Line", lineCount + ":", line)
        }
    }

    Log("Total lines:", lineCount)
    file.close()
}
```

Used to determine whether all content has been read when reading a file. It returns ```true``` only after a read has hit the end of file, e.g. ```getline()``` returned ```undefined```, ```read(size)``` got no data, or ```read()``` without arguments read the rest of the file; ```seek()``` resets it to ```false```.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.read`, `File.getline`

##### File.read

```
read()
read(size)
```

Read data from a file.

Parameters:

- `size` (number, optional): Number of bytes to read. If not specified, reads all remaining content in the file.

Returns (string / ArrayBuffer): Returns the content read. At the end of file it returns an empty string ```""``` (an empty ```ArrayBuffer``` in ```b``` mode).

Read file content in chunks.

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("data.txt", "r")

    // data.txt
    // This is a test line: Line 1.
    // This is a test line: Line 2.
    // ...

    let chunkSize = 29
    let totalBytes = 0

    while (!file.eof()) {
        let chunk = file.read(chunkSize)
        if (chunk) {
            totalBytes += chunk.length || chunk.byteLength
            Log("Read chunk, total bytes so far:", totalBytes, ", chunk:", chunk)
        }
    }

    file.close()
}
```

Can read a specified number of bytes or all remaining content in the file. Returns an ```ArrayBuffer``` when the file was opened in ```b``` mode (e.g. ```"rb"```), otherwise a string. After reading the rest without a size argument, or after a read that finds no more data, ```eof()``` returns ```true```.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.getline`, `File.eof`, `File.seek`

##### File.write

```
write(data)
```

Write string data to a file.

Parameters:

- `data` (string, required): The string data to be written.

Returns (number): Returns the actual number of bytes written.

Writing trade records

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("trades.log", "a")
    let timestamp = new Date().toISOString()
    let tradeInfo = `${timestamp},BUY,50000,1\n`
    let bytes = file.write(tradeInfo)
    Log("Trade record written, bytes:", bytes)
    file.close()
}
```

Writes string data to the current position in the file.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.puts`, `File.flush`

##### File.getline

```
getline()
```

Read the next line from the file.

Returns (string / undefined): Returns the next line (without the line break); returns ```undefined``` once all content has been read. An empty line in the file returns an empty string ```""```.

Read file line by line until the end.

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("data.txt", "r")
    let lineCount = 0

    let line
    while ((line = file.getline()) !== undefined) {
        lineCount++
        Log("Line", lineCount + ":", line)
    }

    Log("Total lines:", lineCount)
    file.close()
}
```

Read file content line by line in sequential order.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.read`, `File.eof`

##### File.toString

```
toString()
```

Get the string representation of the file object.

Returns (string): Returns the string description information of the file object.

Get the description information of the file object.

```javascript
function main() {
    let file = os.open("data/data.txt", "r")
    Log("File info:", file.toString())
    // Output: File info: File(data/data.txt)
    file.close()
}
```

Returns the description information of the file object.

See also: `File`, `os.open`, `File.read`

#### ListFilesResult

File list object used to record directory listing information. This object contains two array properties: ```files``` (file list) and ```dirs``` (directory list).

ListFilesResult object structure:

```javascript
{
    files: string[],  // Array of searched file names
    dirs: string[]    // Array of subdirectory names in the current directory
}
```

This object is returned by the ```os.listFiles()``` function.

See also: `File`, `os`, `FileStat`

#### FileStat

File statistics information object.

FileStat object structure:

```javascript
{
    size: number,   // File size (bytes)
    mode: number,   // File mode (the low 9 bits are the permission bits; 420 for a regular 0644 file)
    mtime: number,  // Modification time, millisecond timestamp
    atime: number,  // Millisecond timestamp, currently the same as mtime
    ctime: number   // Millisecond timestamp, currently the same as mtime
}
```

This object is returned by the ```os.stat()``` function.

See also: `File`, `os`, `ListFilesResult`

## Structures

Structures are the data returned by API functions: tickers, depth, trades, K-lines, market information, orders, conditional orders, accounts, assets, positions and funding rates, plus function options and returned objects (`Other Structures`).

The ```Info``` field of a structure holds the raw data from the exchange API (absent in backtests); read it when a standard field is missing. Functions that return a structure return a null value on failure, see `Failures and Null Values`.

### Ticker

Market data structure.

Fields:

- `Info` (object): Raw data returned by the exchange API, not included in backtesting.
- `Symbol` (string): The FMZ symbol, written as described in `Symbols`, for example ```BTC_USDT``` on spot and ```BTC_USDT.swap``` (USDT-margined perpetual) on futures, and ```BTC_USDT.BTC-240108-40000-C``` for an option (a call with strike 40000 expiring on 8 January 2024).
- `High` (number): Highest price. May be 0 if the exchange API does not provide the 24-hour high; some exchanges approximate it with the best ask price.
- `Low` (number): Lowest price. May be 0 if the exchange API does not provide the 24-hour low; some exchanges approximate it with the best bid price.
- `Sell` (number): Current best ask price. Some exchanges' ticker endpoints carry no order book data, in which case it is 0; use `exchange.GetDepth` when you need order book prices.
- `Buy` (number): Current best bid price. It is 0 when the exchange's ticker endpoint carries no order book data.
- `Last` (number): Last traded price.
- `Open` (number): Period opening price. May be 0 if the exchange API does not provide the opening price for the 24-hour rolling period.
- `Volume` (number): Recent trading volume. In principle, spot trading volume is in base currency units, and contract trading volume is in contract units. If the exchange API does not provide such data, it is filled with available data from the exchange API, for example, it may be trading volume in quote currency units.
- `Time` (number): Timestamp in milliseconds.
- `OpenInterest` (number): Open interest. Most exchange APIs do not provide this data, and the value is 0 when not supported.

The exchange.GetTicker() function returns a Ticker structure.

For option contracts, the order book is usually thin and there are often no orders on the bid or ask side; in that case the ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` fields of the ```Ticker``` structure are 0, and ```Last``` may also be 0 for an option that has never traded. Some exchanges report the mark price as ```Last``` (always, or only when there is no last trade price); see the "Options" and "Notes" sections of each exchange page. Check these fields before using option market data.

See also: `exchange.GetTicker`, `exchange.GetTickers`

### Depth

Market depth data structure.

Fields:

- `Info` (object): Raw data returned by the exchange API, not included in backtesting.
- `Asks` (array): Ask orders array, i.e., OrderBook array, sorted by price from low to high, with the first OrderBook structure in the array having the lowest price.
- `Bids` (array): Bid orders array, i.e., OrderBook array, sorted by price from high to low, with the first OrderBook structure in the array having the highest price.
- `Time` (number): Timestamp in milliseconds.

The exchange.GetDepth() function returns a Depth structure.

See also: `exchange.GetDepth`, `OrderBook`

### OrderBook

Order structure in market depth.

Fields:

- `Price` (number): Order price.
- `Amount` (number): Order quantity.

In the data structure returned by the exchange.GetDepth() function, the attribute values of Bids and Asks are OrderBook arrays.

See also: `exchange.GetDepth`, `Depth`

### Trade

Data structure for market trade records.

Fields:

- `Id` (string): Unique identifier for the market trade record. If the exchange API does not provide an Id, the platform generates one (either a timestamp or a synthetic string starting with ```syn:```), which is only guaranteed to be unique within a single result.
- `Time` (number): Timestamp in milliseconds.
- `Price` (number): Execution price.
- `Amount` (number): Execution quantity.
- `Type` (number): Order type, refer to `ORDER_TYPE_BUY`, `ORDER_TYPE_SELL`. It is ```2``` when the exchange does not report the trade direction and it cannot be determined, so do not treat "not a sell" as "a buy".

The exchange.GetTrades() function returns an array of Trade; it is an empty array when there is no data, and a null value (```null``` in JavaScript, ```None``` in Python) when the call fails.

See also: `exchange.GetTrades`

### Record

Data structure for candlestick bars in standard OHLC format, used for charting candlesticks and calculating technical indicators.

Fields:

- `Time` (number): Millisecond timestamp representing the start time of this candlestick period.
- `Open` (number): Opening price.
- `High` (number): Highest price.
- `Low` (number): Lowest price.
- `Close` (number): Closing price.
- `OpenInterest` (number): Open interest. Most exchange APIs do not provide this data; value is 0 when not supported.
- `Volume` (number): Trading volume. For spot trading, volume is principally in base currency units; for futures, volume is in contract units. If the exchange API does not provide standard data, existing API data is used for filling, which may be volume in quote currency units.

The exchange.GetRecords() function returns an array of Records; it is an empty array when there is no data, and a null value (```null``` in JavaScript, ```None``` in Python) when the call fails. Each Record structure represents one candlestick bar.

For Python, different versions of pandas packages may require different handling, for example:

```python
pandas.DataFrame(records)  # May need to be adjusted to: pandas.DataFrame(list(records))
```

Related error message: ```in getattr KeyError: 'dtype'```.

See also: `exchange.GetRecords`

### Market

Data structure for trading symbol market information.

Fields:

- `Symbol` (string): Example value: ```"btcusdt"```, the ```Symbol``` field records the original name of this trading symbol on the exchange. Note that the format and definition of this attribute differs from the ```Symbol``` field in the `Ticker` structure.
- `BaseAsset` (string): Example value: ```"BTC"```, the ```BaseAsset``` field records the base currency name (i.e., baseCurrency), uniformly in uppercase letters.
- `QuoteAsset` (string): Example value: ```"USDT"```, the ```QuoteAsset``` field records the quote currency name (i.e., quoteCurrency), uniformly in uppercase letters.
- `TickSize` (number): Example value: ```0.01```, the ```TickSize``` field records the minimum price increment for this trading symbol on the exchange.
- `AmountSize` (number): Example value: ```0.01```, the ```AmountSize``` field records the minimum order quantity increment for this trading symbol on the exchange.
- `PricePrecision` (number): Example value: ```2```, the ```PricePrecision``` field records the price precision for this trading symbol on the exchange, indicating the price is accurate to 2 decimal places. The value can be negative: for example, with a price tick of 10 it is ```-1```, meaning prices are rounded to the tens place.
- `AmountPrecision` (number): Example value: ```3```, the ```AmountPrecision``` field records the order quantity precision for this trading symbol on the exchange, indicating the order quantity is accurate to 3 decimal places. Like ```PricePrecision```, the value can be negative.
- `MinQty` (number): Example value: ```0.001```, the ```MinQty``` field records the minimum order quantity for this trading symbol on the exchange.
- `MaxQty` (number): Example value: ```1000```, the ```MaxQty``` field records the maximum order quantity for this trading symbol on the exchange. When the exchange does not provide a maximum order quantity, the value is ```9007199254740991``` (2^53−1), meaning no limit.
- `MinNotional` (number): Example value: ```5```, the ```MinNotional``` field records the minimum order value for this trading symbol on the exchange.
- `MaxNotional` (number): Example value: ```9999999```, the ```MaxNotional``` field records the maximum order value for this trading symbol on the exchange. When the exchange does not provide a maximum order value, it is usually ```9007199254740991``` (2^53−1), meaning no limit; some exchange objects omit this field.
- `CtVal` (number): The ```CtVal``` field records the value corresponding to a single contract for this trading symbol on the exchange, with the unit specified in the ```CtValCcy``` field. For example: ```CtVal``` of 0.01 and ```CtValCcy``` of ```"BTC"``` means a single contract is worth 0.01 BTC.
- `CtValCcy` (string): The ```CtValCcy``` field records the value unit of a single contract. The value unit of a single contract can be: ```BTC```, ```USD```, ```ETH```, etc.
- `Info` (object): The ```Info``` field records the raw data of this symbol returned by the exchange's market information interface.

The exchange.GetMarkets() function returns a dictionary containing this ```Market``` structure.

Exchanges differ in how much market information they provide, so note the following: ```MaxQty``` and ```MaxNotional``` are ```9007199254740991``` (meaning no limit) when the exchange does not provide them; ```MaxNotional```, ```CtVal``` and ```CtValCcy``` are omitted when there is no data (spot symbols usually have no ```CtVal```/```CtValCcy```; the Rust ```Market``` structure always has these fields, which are then ```0``` or an empty string); ```PricePrecision``` and ```AmountPrecision``` can be negative; exchanges without a market list endpoint cannot provide the native name, in which case ```Symbol``` is the FMZ trading symbol code (such as ```BTC_USDT```). All field values above are derived from the exchange interface's raw data, and specific details can also be found in the ```Info``` field content.

See also: `exchange.GetMarkets`

### Order

Order structure.

Fields:

- `Info` (object): Raw data returned by the exchange interface, this attribute is not available during backtesting.
- `Symbol` (string): The FMZ symbol, written as described in `Symbols`, for example ```BTC_USDT``` on spot and ```BTC_USDT.swap``` (USDT-margined perpetual) on futures; the same format as ```Symbol``` of `Ticker`.
- `Id` (string): Order ID. On most exchanges the order ID consists of the exchange symbol code and the exchange's original order ID, separated by an English comma. For example, the ```Id``` attribute format for an ```ETH_USDT``` spot trading pair order on OKX exchange is: ```ETH-USDT,1547130415509278720```. On a few exchanges the order ID is just the exchange's original order ID without the symbol code. Treat ```Id``` as an opaque string and pass it on unchanged (for example to ```exchange.CancelOrder()```); do not split or build it yourself.
- `Price` (number): Order price, note that this attribute for market orders may be 0 or -1.
- `Amount` (number): Order quantity, note that this attribute for market orders may be the amount value rather than the coin quantity.
- `DealAmount` (number): Filled quantity, if the exchange interface does not provide this data, it may be filled with 0.
- `AvgPrice` (number): Average filled price, note that some exchanges do not provide this data. When not provided and cannot be calculated, this attribute is set to 0.
- `Status` (number): Order status, refer to `ORDER_STATE_PENDING`, `ORDER_STATE_CLOSED`, `ORDER_STATE_CANCELED`, `ORDER_STATE_UNKNOWN`.
- `Type` (number): Order type, refer to `ORDER_TYPE_BUY`, `ORDER_TYPE_SELL`.
- `Offset` (number): Open/close direction for contract orders, refer to `ORDER_OFFSET_OPEN`, `ORDER_OFFSET_CLOSE`.
- `ContractType` (string): For spot orders, this attribute is ```""```, i.e., an empty string. For contract orders, this attribute is the specific contract code.
- `Condition` (object): Trigger conditions and order prices of a conditional order, see `Condition`. Ordinary orders have no such field; see the remarks for how to read it in each language.
- `Time` (number): Order creation time, millisecond timestamp.

The ```Order``` structure can be returned by ```exchange.GetOrder()``` and ```exchange.GetOrders()``` functions. The ```exchange.GetOrders()``` function returns an array of ```Order``` structures. If there are no pending orders currently, it returns ```[]```, i.e., an empty array; if the call fails (network error, exchange error, etc.), it returns a null value (```null``` in JavaScript, ```None``` in Python). The ```Status``` attribute of the ```Order``` structure can be directly compared with constants like ```ORDER_STATE_PENDING``` to determine if they are equal and thus confirm the order status.

For one-way position mode, when it cannot be determined whether an order is for closing (reducing) a position, the ```Offset``` field is set to the opening direction by default, i.e., ```ORDER_OFFSET_OPEN```.

The ```Time``` field represents the order creation time as a millisecond timestamp. Some exchanges may also include time information in the ```Info``` field, but the ```Time``` field provides a standardized timestamp format.

Ordinary orders have no ```Condition``` field: in JavaScript reading it gives ```undefined```; in Python the key is absent, so accessing ```order.Condition``` as an attribute raises ```AttributeError```; use ```order.get("Condition")``` or ```"Condition" in order```; in Rust the ```Order``` structure always has ```Condition```, and for an ordinary order ```Condition.ConditionType``` is ```-1```.

See also: `exchange.GetOrder`, `exchange.GetOrders`, `exchange.GetHistoryOrders`, `Condition`

### Condition

Conditional order configuration structure, used to set trigger conditions and execution prices for conditional orders.

Fields:

- `ConditionType` (number): Conditional order type, see `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE`: OCO (```0```), take-profit (```1```), stop-loss (```2```) or generic (```3```, only in query results).
- `TpTriggerPrice` (number): Take profit trigger price. Used when the conditional order type is TP or OCO, the take profit order is triggered when the market price reaches this price.
- `TpOrderPrice` (number): Take profit order execution price, i.e., the actual order price after take profit is triggered. When placing the order, a price of -1 means execution as a market order; in conditional orders returned by queries, this price is usually 0 for market execution.
- `SlTriggerPrice` (number): Stop loss trigger price. Used when the conditional order type is SL or OCO, the stop loss order is triggered when the market price reaches this price.
- `SlOrderPrice` (number): Stop loss order execution price, i.e., the actual order price after stop loss is triggered. When placing the order, a price of -1 means execution as a market order; in conditional orders returned by queries, this price is usually 0 for market execution.

- OCO orders (ConditionType=`ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_OCO`) set both take profit and stop loss conditions simultaneously. When one condition is triggered, the other is automatically canceled.
- TP orders (ConditionType=`ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_TP`) only use the TpTriggerPrice and TpOrderPrice fields.
- SL orders (ConditionType=`ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_SL`) only use the SlTriggerPrice and SlOrderPrice fields.
- GENERIC orders (ConditionType=`ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_GENERIC`) are generic conditional orders, and the specific fields used depend on the exchange implementation. In GENERIC orders returned by queries, the Tp* and Sl* field groups hold the same values (one trigger price and one order price). The GENERIC type only appears in query results; `exchange.CreateConditionOrder` and `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder` do not support it and return a null value with an error logged.

Support for conditional order functionality depends on the specific exchange. Some exchanges may not support certain types of conditional orders.

See also: `Order`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrder`

### Account

Data structure for account information.

Fields:

- `Info` (object): Raw data returned by the exchange API. This property does not exist in backtesting mode.
- `Balance` (number): Available amount of quote currency. In spot trading, if the trading pair is BTC_USDT, Balance represents the current available USDT amount. In USDT-margined contracts, Balance represents the available margin (USDT, quoteCurrency) amount.
- `FrozenBalance` (number): Asset value frozen when orders are pending.
- `Stocks` (number): Available amount of base currency. In spot trading, if the trading pair is BTC_USDT, Stocks represents the current available BTC amount. In coin-margined contracts, Stocks represents the available margin (coin, baseCurrency) amount.
- `FrozenStocks` (number): Asset value frozen when orders are pending.
- `Equity` (number): Only supported by futures exchange objects. The ```Equity``` field represents the **total equity** of the futures account margin under the current contract settings. If the exchange API does not provide relevant data, this field value is 0.
- `UPnL` (number): Only supported by futures exchange objects. The ```UPnL``` field represents the total **unrealized profit and loss** of all open positions in the futures account margin under the current contract settings.

The exchange.GetAccount() function returns an Account structure. The data in the returned structure depends on the currently set trading pair and contract code.

See also: `exchange.GetAccount`

### Asset

Data structure for specific currency asset information.

Fields:

- `Currency` (string): Currency asset name defined by the exchange. Due to potential differences in naming conventions across exchanges, the same currency may use different identifiers on different exchanges, for example ```BTC``` may be identified as ```XBT``` on some exchanges.
- `Amount` (number): Available balance amount of the currency asset.
- `FrozenAmount` (number): Frozen amount of the currency asset.

The frozen amount ```FrozenAmount``` of currency assets typically includes assets locked by open orders and margin required for futures positions.

See also: `exchange.GetAssets`

### Position

Data structure for contract position information.

Fields:

- `Info` (object): Raw data returned by the exchange interface. This attribute does not exist in backtesting mode.
- `Symbol` (string): The FMZ symbol, written as described in `Symbols`, for example ```BTC_USDT``` on spot and ```BTC_USDT.swap``` (USDT-margined perpetual) on futures; the same format as ```Symbol``` of `Ticker`.
- `MarginLevel` (number): Position leverage multiplier. If the exchange interface does not provide this data, it will be filled through calculation and may contain errors.
- `Amount` (number): Position quantity, usually a positive integer (number of contracts). Note that contract multipliers, values, and other contract specifications may differ between exchanges.
- `FrozenAmount` (number): Frozen position quantity, temporarily frozen position quantity when close orders are not filled.
- `Price` (number): Average position price. In principle, this attribute is the overall average price of the position (not involved in settlement). If the exchange interface does not provide this data, it will be filled with the existing average position price from the exchange interface (involved in settlement).
- `Profit` (number): Floating profit and loss of the position. In principle, this is the unrealized profit and loss of the position. If the exchange interface does not provide this data, it will be filled with other profit and loss data from the exchange interface. The unit of the profit and loss value is the same as the unit of the current contract margin.
- `Type` (number): Position type, refer to `PD_LONG`, `PD_SHORT`.
- `ContractType` (string): Contract code. For specific content, please refer to the description of the `exchange.SetContractType` function.
- `Margin` (number): Margin occupied by the position. If the exchange interface does not provide this data, it will be filled with 0.

The exchange.GetPositions() function returns a Position array; it is an empty array when there are no positions, and a null value (```null``` in JavaScript, ```None``` in Python) when the call fails.

For cryptocurrency futures, it should be noted that in the Position structure array returned by the exchange.GetPositions() function, the FrozenAmount, Profit, and Margin attributes of the position data structure may have different definitions when calling the exchange.GetPositions() interface for different exchange objects, as the data provided by exchanges is not unified.

For example, some exchanges do not have frozen position data in their position data, in which case FrozenAmount is 0. If specific data needs to be calculated, the raw data in the Info attribute can be used for calculation and analysis.

See also: `exchange.GetPositions`

### Funding

Data structure for trading instrument funding rate information, only cryptocurrency perpetual contracts support funding rate functionality.

Fields:

- `Info` (object): Raw data object returned from cryptocurrency futures exchange funding rate API calls.
- `Symbol` (string): The ```Symbol``` field is the standardized trading instrument code defined by the FMZ platform.
- `Interval` (number): Funding rate settlement interval period, unit: milliseconds. For example, ```28800000``` represents an 8-hour interval.
- `Time` (number): Timestamp of the next funding rate period start time (current period settlement time), unit: milliseconds.
- `Rate` (number): Funding rate value to be applied at the current period settlement.

Different futures exchanges use different calculation methods and mechanisms for perpetual contract funding rates, with settlement periods including 1 hour, 4 hours, 8 hours, 24 hours, etc.

The current funding rate for futures exchange perpetual contracts may be a fixed value or a real-time calculated floating value.

The ```Rate``` field is the funding rate value without the ```%``` symbol. To convert to percentage format, multiply the value by 100 and add the ```%``` symbol.

See also: `exchange.GetFundings`

### Other Structures

Option objects of functions, and objects or structures they return (connection, chart and concurrent objects, button structures, etc.).

#### HttpQuery-options

This JSON structure is used to configure various parameters for HTTP requests sent by HttpQuery and HttpQuery_Go functions.

Fields:

- `method` (string): HTTP request method, for example: ```GET```, ```POST```, etc.
- `body` (string): Request body content. For example, in POST requests, body can contain form data, JSON data, text, etc.
- `charset` (string): Character set of the response. When set, the response body is decoded from this character set into UTF-8 text, for example ```"GBK"``` for a GBK-encoded web page. ```Length``` in the returned structure is still the length before decoding; an unrecognized character set logs an error and leaves the body unchanged. This option has nothing to do with the encoding of the request body.
- `cookie` (string): Cookie is a small piece of data used to store and exchange state information between the client (usually a browser) and the server.
- `debug` (bool): Debug mode switch. When set to true, the HttpQuery function call will return the complete HTTP response message; when set to false, it only returns the data in the response message Body.
- `headers` (object): HTTP request header information, existing as key-value pairs (JSON structure), used to pass various information such as content type, authentication information, cache control, etc.
- `proxy` (string): Proxy for this request. Supports ```http://```, ```https://```, ```socks5://``` and ```socks5h://```, for example: ```"socks5://user:pass@127.0.0.1:1080"```. It applies only to this request and is independent of the exchange proxy set by ```exchange.SetProxy()```.
- `timeout` (number): Timeout setting in milliseconds. Setting 1000 means 1 second timeout. Defaults to 300000 (5 minutes) when not set.

Usage example:
```javascript
function main() {
    var options = {
        method: "POST",
        body: "a=10&b=20&c=30",
        charset: "UTF-8",
        cookie: "session_id=12345; lang=en",
        debug: false,
        headers: {"TEST-HTTP-QUERY": "123"},
        timeout: 1000
    }
    var ret = HttpQuery("http://127.0.0.1:8080", options)
    Log(ret)
}
```

HTTP message sent when the above code is executed:

```log
POST / HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: session_id=12345; lang=en
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
Test-Http-Query: 123
Content-Length: 14
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ...
Accept-Encoding: gzip, br

a=10&b=20&c=30

```

See also: `HttpQuery`, `HttpQuery_Go`

#### HttpQuery-return

This JSON structure is the data structure returned by the HttpQuery function in debug mode, when the debug field is set to true in the ```options``` parameter structure while calling the HttpQuery function.

Fields:

- `StatusCode` (number): HTTP status code. It is 0 when no response is received for the request (connection refused, DNS resolution failure, timeout, proxy failure, etc.).
- `Header` (object): Response header information. The value of each key is an array of strings (a header name can appear several times, for example multiple ```Set-Cookie``` headers).
- `Cookies` (array): Array parsed from each ```Set-Cookie``` header of the response; every element has the fields ```Name```, ```Value```, ```Path```, ```Domain```, ```Expires```, ```MaxAge```, ```Secure```, ```HttpOnly```, ```SameSite``` and ```Raw```.
- `Trace` (object): Diagnostic timing information for each stage of the request, including millisecond values such as ```elapsed_ms``` (total), ```dns_ms```, ```connect_ms```, ```tls_ms```, ```ttfb_ms``` (time to first byte) and ```recv_ms```, plus fields such as ```peer_addr``` (remote address), ```reused``` (whether the connection was reused) and ```version``` (HTTP version). Only present when ```debug``` is true.
- `Length` (number): Message length. When ```charset``` is set, it is the length before decoding.
- `Body` (string): Message content. It is an empty string when the request fails.
- `Error` (string): The reason for the request failure, including the request method, URL, and underlying error information, for example: ```Get "https://www.okx.com/api/v5/public/time": timeout after 1000ms```. It only appears when the request fails (```StatusCode``` is 0).

Example of the returned JSON data structure:
```json
{
    "StatusCode": 302,
    "Header": {
        "Content-Type": ["text/html"],
        "Location": ["https://www.example.com/"]
    },
    "Cookies": [],
    "Trace": {
        "elapsed_ms": 152.4,
        "dns_ms": 3.1,
        "connect_ms": 20.5,
        "tls_ms": 45.2,
        "ttfb_ms": 150.8,
        "recv_ms": 1.6,
        "peer_addr": "93.184.216.34:443",
        "reused": false,
        "version": "HTTP/1.1"
    },
    "Length": 154,
    "Body": "..."
}
```

Example of the data structure returned when the request fails (no response received):
```json
{
    "StatusCode": 0,
    "Header": {},
    "Cookies": [],
    "Length": 0,
    "Body": "",
    "Error": "Get \"https://www.okx.com/api/v5/public/time\": timeout after 1000ms"
}
```
Responses with HTTP status codes 4xx and 5xx are not considered request failures. In this case, ```StatusCode``` is the actual status code, and the ```Error``` field is not included. You can use ```StatusCode``` for unified checking: ```if (ret.StatusCode !== 200) { ... }```.

In Rust, the ```HttpRet``` structure returned by ```HttpQuery``` only has the fields ```StatusCode```, ```Header```, ```Cookies```, ```Body``` and ```Error``` (there is no ```Length``` or ```Trace```, and ```Cookies``` is not filled).

See also: `HttpQuery`, `HttpQuery_Go`

#### LogStatus-table

This JSON structure is used to configure the table content displayed in the strategy status bar.

Fields:

- `type` (string): Used to set the type of UI control to be parsed and displayed. For status bar tables, it is fixed as: ```table```.
- `title` (string): Used to set the title of the status bar table.
- `cols` (array): Used to set the column headers of the status bar table. The first element of the array is the title of the first column, and so on.
- `rows` (array): Used to set the row data of the status bar table. The first element of this rows array (two-dimensional array) is also an array structure. The length of this array structure should be consistent with the number of table columns (elements in the array correspond one-to-one with table column names), representing the first row of data in the table.

```javascript
function main() {
    var tbl = {
        type: "table",
        title: "Title",
        cols: ["Column 1", "Column 2", "Column 3"],
        rows: [
            ["Row 1 Col 1", "Row 1 Col 2", "Row 1 Col 3"],
            ["Row 2 Col 1", "Row 2 Col 2", "Row 2 Col 3"],
            ["Row 3 Col 1", "Row 3 Col 2", "Row 3 Col 3"],
        ]
    }
    LogStatus("`" + JSON.stringify(tbl) + "`")
}
```

See also: `LogStatus`

#### LogStatus-btnTypeOne

Older form of the status bar button structure (input controls without ```settings```), still supported. New code should use `LogStatus-btnTypeTwo`; the field reference is under "Status bar buttons" in `LogStatus`.

A button can be output to the status bar on its own or embedded in a status bar table.
