The controls in the popup shown after a click are configured with ```input``` (one control) or ```group``` (a group of controls), and what is submitted is received by `GetCommand`. For example, a button that pops up a number input:

```json
{
    "type": "button",
    "cmd": "open",
    "name": "Open Position",
    "input": {
        "name": "Position Size",
        "type": "number",
        "defValue": 1
    }
}
```

Fields:

- `type` (string): For button controls, fixed as: ```button```.
- `class` (string): Button style, a Bootstrap button class name such as ```"btn btn-xs btn-danger"```; see the remarks for examples.
- `name` (string): The text displayed on the button control, i.e., the button name.
- `cmd` (string): The interactive command content sent to the strategy when the button control triggers a click operation.
- `description` (string): Description information for the button control. This description is displayed when the mouse hovers over the button in the status bar.
- `disabled` (bool): Set the button as disabled (true) or enabled (false).
- `input` (object): The input control in the popup shown after the button is clicked; see the "```input``` fields" table in the remarks.
- `group` (array): A group of controls in the popup shown after the button is clicked; each element has the same structure as ```input```.

Fields of ```input``` (each element of ```group``` is the same):

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| ```name``` | Title of the control in the popup. |
| ```description``` | Description of the control in the popup. |
| ```type``` | Control type: ```"number"``` number input, ```"string"``` string input, ```"selected"``` drop-down, ```"boolean"``` switch. |
| ```defValue``` | Default value of the control. A drop-down can list its options here, separated by vertical bars; when ```options``` is set it is the default option, an array for multiple selection. |
| ```options``` | Options of a drop-down: strings or ```{text: "label", value: "value"}``` objects. |
| ```multiple``` | When ```true```, the drop-down allows multiple selection. |

Example of ```class``` attribute values for button JSON structure in status bar:
```javascript
function main() {
    var table = {
        type: "table",
        title: "Status Bar Button Styles",
        cols: ["Default", "Primary", "Success", "Info", "Warning", "Danger"],
        rows: [
            [
                {"type":"button", "class": "btn btn-xs btn-default", "name": "Default"},
                {"type":"button", "class": "btn btn-xs btn-primary", "name": "Primary"},
                {"type":"button", "class": "btn btn-xs btn-success", "name": "Success"},
                {"type":"button", "class": "btn btn-xs btn-info", "name": "Info"},
                {"type":"button", "class": "btn btn-xs btn-warning", "name": "Warning"},
                {"type":"button", "class": "btn btn-xs btn-danger", "name": "Danger"}
            ]
        ]
    }
    LogStatus("`" + JSON.stringify(table) + "`")
}
```

```group``` field and ```input``` field usage example:
```javascript
function main() {
    // Status bar button control (implemented with input field) - The dropdown control on the page triggered by testBtn1 button uses options field to set options and defValue field to set default option. This differs from other examples in this chapter that directly use defValue to set options.
    var testBtn1 = {
        type: "button",
        name: "testBtn1",
        cmd: "cmdTestBtn1",
        input: {name: "testBtn1ComboBox", type: "selected", options: ["A", "B"], defValue: 1}
    }

    /*
      Status bar button control (implemented with input field) - The dropdown control on the page triggered by testBtn2 button uses options field to set options. The options field supports not only strings,
      but also ```{text: "description", value: "value"}``` structure. Use defValue field to set default option, which can be multiple selections (implemented through array structure). Multiple selection requires setting additional field multiple to true.
    */
    var testBtn2 = {
        type: "button",
        name: "testBtn2",
        cmd: "cmdTestBtn2",
        input: {
            name: "testBtn2MultiComboBox",
            type: "selected",
            description: "Implement dropdown multi-select",
            options: [{text: "Option A", value: "A"}, {text: "Option B", value: "B"}, {text: "Option C", value: "C"}],
            defValue: ["A", "C"],
            multiple: true
        }
    }

    // Status bar grouped button control (implemented with group field) - The dropdown control on the page triggered by testBtn3 button uses options field to set options, and also supports directly using defValue to set options.
    var testBtn3 = {
        type: "button",
        name: "testBtn3",
        cmd: "cmdTestBtn3",
        group: [
            {name: "comboBox1", label: "labelComboBox1", description: "Dropdown 1", type: "selected", defValue: 1, options: ["A", "B"]},
            {name: "comboBox2", label: "labelComboBox2", description: "Dropdown 2", type: "selected", defValue: "A|B"},
            {name: "comboBox3", label: "labelComboBox3", description: "Dropdown 3", type: "selected", defValue: [0, 2], multiple: true, options: ["A", "B", "C"]},
            {
                name: "comboBox4",
                label: "labelComboBox4",
                description: "Dropdown 4",
                type: "selected",
                defValue: ["A", "C"],
                multiple: true,
                options: [{text: "Option A", value: "A"}, {text: "Option B", value: "B"}, {text: "Option C", value: "C"}, {text: "Option D", value: "D"}]
            }
        ]
    }
    while (true) {
        LogStatus("`" + JSON.stringify(testBtn1) + "`\n", "`" + JSON.stringify(testBtn2) + "`\n", "`" + JSON.stringify(testBtn3) + "`\n")
        var cmd = GetCommand()
        if (cmd) {
            Log(cmd)
        }
        Sleep(5000)
    }
}
```

See also: `LogStatus`

#### LogStatus-btnTypeTwo

JSON structure of a status bar button (current form, with ```settings``` on input controls). A button can be output directly to the status bar or placed in a status bar table cell. The full description of the fields, the command format and ```settings``` is under "Status bar buttons" in `LogStatus`.

For example, a button that opens a group of input controls (```price``` is shown only when a limit order is selected); after confirming, ```GetCommand()``` receives ```open:{"tradeType":1,"direction":"buy","price":60000,"amount":1}```:
```json
{
    "type": "button",
    "cmd": "open",
    "name": "开仓|Open",
    "group": [{
        "type": "selected",
        "name": "tradeType",
        "label": "下单类型|Order type",
        "default": 0,
        "settings": {"options": ["市价单|Market", "限价单|Limit"]}
    }, {
        "type": "selected",
        "name": "direction",
        "label": "方向|Direction",
        "default": "buy",
        "settings": {"render": "segment", "options": [{"name": "买入|Buy", "value": "buy"}, {"name": "卖出|Sell", "value": "sell"}]}
    }, {
        "type": "number",
        "name": "price",
        "label": "价格|Price",
        "required": true,
        "settings": {"filter": "tradeType==1"}
    }, {
        "type": "number",
        "name": "amount",
        "label": "数量|Amount",
        "required": true
    }]
}
```

Fields:

- `type` (string): Always ```"button"```.
- `name` (string): Text on the button.
- `cmd` (string): Command sent to the strategy on click, read with ```GetCommand()```.
- `description` (string): Hint shown on mouse hover.
- `disabled` (bool): ```true``` disables the button.
- `class` (string): Button style, for example ```"btn btn-xs btn-danger"```.
- `input` (object): One input control opened on click: ```type```, ```name```, ```label```, ```description```, ```default```, ```required```, ```settings```. The command is ```cmd:value```.
- `group` (array): A group of input controls opened on click; each item has the structure of ```input```, and ```name``` is the key of the control in the command JSON. The command is ```cmd:JSON```.

See also: `LogStatus`, `LogStatus-btnTypeOne`, `GetCommand`

#### Chart-options

This JSON is used to configure chart settings for the custom plotting function ```Chart()```. The chart library uses Highcharts. The following lists several basic configuration fields.

Fields:

- `__isStock` (bool): Platform extension field. When set to true, uses Highstocks chart; when set to false, uses Highcharts chart.
- `extension` (object): Platform extension: with ```layout``` ```"single"``` the chart is shown on its own instead of in the group (default ```"group"```); ```height``` is the chart height, for example ```{"layout": "single", "height": 300}```.
- `title` (object): Chart title, an object, for example: ```{text: "Spread Analysis Chart"}```.
- `xAxis` (object): X-axis configuration.
- `yAxis` (object): Y-axis configuration.
- `series` (object): Chart data series.

Simple plotting example:
```javascript
// This chart is an object in JavaScript. Before using the Chart function, you need to declare an object variable chart for configuring the chart
var chart = {
    // This field marks whether the chart is a stock chart. Interested users can change it to false and run to see the effect
    __isStock: true,
    // Hover tooltip
    tooltip: {xDateFormat: '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, %A'},
    // Title
    title : { text : 'Spread Analysis Chart'},
    // Range selector
    rangeSelector: {
        buttons: [{type: 'hour',count: 1, text: '1h'}, {type: 'hour',count: 3, text: '3h'}, {type: 'hour', count: 8, text: '8h'}, {type: 'all',text: 'All'}],
        selected: 0,
        inputEnabled: false
    },
    // Horizontal axis (X-axis), currently set type is datetime
    xAxis: { type: 'datetime'},
    // Vertical axis (Y-axis), default values adjust with data size
    yAxis : {
        // Title
        title: {text: 'Spread'},
        // Whether to enable right-side Y-axis
        opposite: false
    },
    // Data series, this property stores various data series (lines, candlestick charts, labels, etc.)
    series : [
        // Index 0, data array stores data for this index series
        {name : "line1", id : "Line1,buy1Price", data : []},
        // Index 1, dashStyle:'shortdash' is set to display as dashed line
        {name : "line2", id : "Line2,lastPrice", dashStyle : 'shortdash', data : []}
    ]
}
function main(){
    // Call Chart function to initialize the chart
    var ObjChart = Chart(chart)
    // Clear
    ObjChart.reset()
    while(true){
        // Get the timestamp of this polling cycle, i.e., millisecond timestamp, used to determine the position on the chart's X-axis
        var nowTime = new Date().getTime()
        // Get market data
        var ticker = _C(exchange.GetTicker)
        // Get the best bid price from the market data return value
        var buy1Price = ticker.Buy
        // Get the last traded price. To prevent the two lines from overlapping, we add 1
        var lastPrice = ticker.Last + 1
        // Pass timestamp as X value and best bid price as Y value to data series at index 0
        ObjChart.add(0, [nowTime, buy1Price])
        // Same as above
        ObjChart.add(1, [nowTime, lastPrice])
        Sleep(2000)
    }
}
```

See also: `Chart`

#### Chart-return

The chart object returned by `Chart`, used to write data, update the configuration and clear the chart.

Fields:

- `add(series, data, index)` (function): Writes data to the chart. ```series``` is the index of the data series (integer); ```data``` is the data to write (array), for example ```[1574993606000, 13.5]```; the optional ```index``` selects the data point to modify, negative values allowed, ```-1``` being the last point; without it the data is appended to the series. For example, to modify the last point of ```series[0]```: ```chart.add(0, [1574993606000, 13.5], -1)```. In ```Rust``` it is ```add(series, data_json, index)``` and ```index``` is required; a value below 0 appends.
- `update(options)` (function): Replaces the current configuration with a new chart configuration (same as the ```Chart()``` argument). Charts without a time axis (for example ```pie```) are updated by passing the whole configuration to ```update()```.
- `reset(remain)` (function): Clears the chart data; ```remain``` is the number of data points to keep, all are cleared when omitted.
- `del(series)` (function): Deletes the data series at the given index; with an argument of 0 or less, or none, the whole chart (including its configuration) is deleted. In ```Python``` the method is named ```dell()``` (```del``` is a keyword); ```Rust``` has no such method.

See also: `Chart`, `Chart-options`

#### KLineChart-options

This JSON is used to configure the chart settings for the custom drawing function ```KLineChart```. Only a few basic configuration fields are listed below.

Fields:

- `overlay` (bool): Whether to draw on the main chart.
- `xAxis` (object): X-axis configuration parameters.
- `yAxis` (object): Y-axis configuration parameters.
- `candle` (object): Candlestick chart configuration parameters.

Refer to [Topic article on drawing with KLineChart function](https://www.fmz.com/bbs-topic/9482).

See also: `KLineChart`

#### KLineChart-return

The chart object returned by `KLineChart`, which draws on K-lines in a ```Pine```-like way. When iterating over bars, the drawing calls for each bar start with ```begin(bar)``` and end with ```close(bar)```.

Fields:

- `begin(bar)` (function): Starts drawing on one bar (`Record`). The drawing calls for each bar must start with ```begin(bar)``` and end with ```close(bar)```.
- `close(bar)` (function): Ends drawing on the current bar. In ```Rust``` it is ```close()``` without an argument.
- `barcolor(color, offset, editable, show_last, title, display)` (function): Sets the bar color. ```display```: ```"none"``` or ```"all"```.
- `bgcolor(color, offset, editable, show_last, title, display, overlay)` (function): Fills the bar background with the given color. ```display```: ```"none"``` or ```"all"```.
- `plot(series, title, color, linewidth, style, trackprice, histbase, offset, join, editable, show_last, display, overlay)` (function): Plots a data line and returns its number (for ```fill()```). See the remarks for the values of ```style``` and ```display```.
- `fill(plot1, plot2, color, title, editable, show_last, fillgaps, display)` (function): Fills the background between two lines (return values of ```plot()``` or ```hline()```) with a color. ```display```: ```"none"``` or ```"all"```.
- `hline(price, title, color, linestyle, linewidth, editable, display, overlay)` (function): Draws a horizontal line at a fixed price. ```linestyle```: ```"dashed"```, ```"dotted"```, ```"solid"```; ```display```: ```"none"``` or ```"all"```.
- `plotarrow(series, title, colorup, colordown, offset, minheight, maxheight, editable, show_last, display, overlay)` (function): Draws up and down arrows (positive values up, negative down). ```display```: ```"none"``` or ```"all"```.
- `plotshape(series, title, style, location, color, offset, text, textcolor, editable, size, show_last, display, overlay)` (function): Draws a shape. See the remarks for the values of ```style```, ```location```, ```size``` and ```display```.
- `plotchar(series, title, char, location, color, offset, text, textcolor, editable, size, show_last, display, overlay)` (function): Draws a shape with any Unicode character. ```location```, ```size``` and ```display``` take the same values as in ```plotshape()```.
- `plotcandle(open, high, low, close, title, color, wickcolor, editable, show_last, bordercolor, display, overlay)` (function): Draws a candlestick. ```display```: ```"none"``` or ```"all"```.
- `signal(direction, price, qty, id)` (function): Not in Pine: draws a trading signal. ```direction```: ```"long"```, ```"closelong"```, ```"short"```, ```"closeshort"```; ```price``` is the vertical position of the mark; ```qty``` is the quantity; the optional ```id``` replaces the default text (the direction).
- `reset(remain)` (function): Not in Pine: clears the chart data; ```remain``` is the number of data points to keep, all are cleared when omitted. ```Rust``` requires ```remain```.

All parameters after the first can be omitted. ```JavaScript``` cannot pass arguments by name, so use an object ```{name: value}```, for example ```c.fill(h, l, {color: "rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.2)", title: "fill"})``` or ```c.plotshape(bar.Low, {style: "diamond"})```; ```Python``` uses keyword arguments, for example ```c.plotshape(bar.Low, style = "diamond")```; in ```Rust``` the last parameter of each method is a JSON string of options (```"{}"``` for none), for example ```c.plot(bar.High, r#"{"title": "high"}"#)```, and the first parameter of ```plotshape()``` and ```plotchar()``` is a boolean that draws on the bar when true.

Colors can be written as ```"rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.2)"``` or ```"#FF0000"```.

Values for ```plot()```: ```style```: ```"stepline_diamond"```, ```"stepline"```, ```"cross"```, ```"areabr"```, ```"area"```, ```"circles"```, ```"columns"```, ```"histogram"```, ```"linebr"```, ```"line"```; ```display```: ```"none"``` or ```"all"```. A ```NaN``` value (```None``` in ```Python```) leaves the point out, which together with ```"linebr"``` draws a broken line.

Values for ```plotshape()```: ```style```: ```"diamond"```, ```"square"```, ```"label_down"```, ```"label_up"```, ```"arrow_down"```, ```"arrow_up"```, ```"circle"```, ```"flag"```, ```"triangle_down"```, ```"triangle_up"```, ```"cross"```, ```"xcross"```; ```location```: ```"abovebar"```, ```"belowbar"```, ```"top"```, ```"bottom"```, ```"absolute"```; ```size```: ```"10px"```, ```"14px"```, ```"20px"```, ```"40px"```, ```"80px"``` (Pine ```size.tiny```, ```size.small```, ```size.normal```, ```size.large```, ```size.huge```; ```size.auto``` is ```size.small```); ```display```: ```"none"``` or ```"all"```.

See also: `KLineChart`, `KLineChart-options`

#### SetData-data

This JSON is used to set the data to be loaded by the ```exchange.SetData()``` function. This JSON data uses an array structure, where each element is also an array with the format ```[time, data]```.

Fields:

- `time` (number): The timestamp of the data, used to mark the time corresponding to this data entry.
- `data` (string / number / bool / object / array / any): data is the specific data content corresponding to a certain time in the data loaded by the ```exchange.SetData()``` function. When the strategy is running, the ```exchange.GetData()``` function retrieves the data with the corresponding timestamp based on the current time.

Example of loading data in the backtesting system and retrieving data when the strategy backtest is running:
```javascript
/*backtest
start: 2020-01-21 00:00:00
end: 2020-02-12 00:00:00
period: 1d
basePeriod: 1d
exchanges: [{"eid":"Bitfinex","currency":"BTC_USD"}]
*/
function main() {
    exchange.SetData("test", [[1579536000000, _D(1579536000000)], [1579622400000, _D(1579622400000)], [1579708800000, _D(1579708800000)]])
    while(true) {
        Log(exchange.GetData("test"))
        Sleep(1000 * 60 * 60 * 24)
    }
}
```

See also: `exchange.SetData`, `exchange.GetData`

#### EventLoop-return

This JSON is the data structure returned by the ```EventLoop()``` function. The ```EventLoop()``` function monitors the following events: 1. Any WebSocket readable data events; 2. Completion events of concurrent tasks from exchange.Go() and HttpQuery_Go() functions; 3. Message events sent by threads created using the ```threading.Thread()``` function in JavaScript language strategies.

Fields:

- `Seq` (number): Event sequence number.
- `Event` (string): Event name.
- `ThreadId` (number): Event thread ID.
- `Index` (number): Event index.
- `Queue` (number): Number of events still waiting in the queue when this event is returned.
- `Nano` (number): Nanosecond timestamp.

When using the ```exchange.Go()``` function for concurrent requests, the event data structure returned by the ```EventLoop()``` function.
```json
{
    "Seq":1,
    "Event":"Exchange_GetTrades",
    "ThreadId":0,
    "Index":3,
    "Queue":0,
    "Nano":1682068771309583400
}
```

When concurrent execution threads in JavaScript language strategies (created by the ```threading.Thread()``` function) use the thread object's ```postMessage()``` function to send messages, the ```EventLoop()``` function in the receiving thread will monitor the following event data structure:
```json
{
    "Seq":4,
    "Event":"thread",
    "ThreadId":1,
    "Index":0,
    "Queue":0,
    "Nano":1727592066508674000
}
```

Ticker and order events pushed by the exchange (```Event``` is ```"tick"``` or ```"order"```, and ```Index``` is the index of the exchange object) also carry a ```Symbol``` field plus a ```Ticker``` (`Ticker` structure) or ```Order``` (`Order` structure) field.

See also: `EventLoop`

#### exchange.Go-return

The concurrent object returned by `exchange.Go`; its ```wait()``` method returns the result of the concurrent call. The concurrent objects returned by ```HttpQuery_Go()``` and ```Mail_Go()``` also have ```wait()```; their return values are described on those function pages, and calling ```wait()``` again after the result has been taken is handled as in the table below (```HttpQuery_Go``` in ```Python``` returns ```None```).

Fields:

- `wait(timeout)` (function): Waits for and takes the result of the concurrent call. ```timeout``` is in milliseconds: omitted or ```0``` blocks until the task finishes; ```-1``` returns at once; a positive value is the maximum wait.

Once a task has finished, its result is released when the concurrent object is no longer referenced; holding the object without taking the result keeps the result alive. When 2000 concurrent tasks have results not yet taken, a further ```exchange.Go()``` call fails with ```too many routine wait, max is 2000```.

What ```wait()``` returns in each language:

| Situation | JavaScript | Python | Rust |
| - | - | - | - |
| Finished | Return value of the call (```null``` if the call failed) | ```(value, True)```; ```(None, False)``` if the call failed | ```Ok(value)``` |
| Timeout (task not finished) | ```undefined``` | ```(None, False)``` | ```Err``` |
| Called again after the result was taken | Throws ```routine N already finished``` | Logs an error and returns ```(None, False)``` | ```Err``` |

After a timeout ```wait()``` can be called again. In ```JavaScript``` test for a timeout with ```typeof(r) === "undefined"```, because ```null == undefined``` is true.

See also: `exchange.Go`, `EventLoop`, `HttpQuery_Go`

#### DBExec-return

This JSON is the data structure returned by the ```DBExec()``` function; this JSON data structure is also returned when executing SQL statements using the ```exec()``` method of objects created by the ```Dial()``` function.

Fields:

- `columns` (array): Column names of the queried data, string array.
- `values` (array): The specific data queried, where each data item corresponds to the column names. The values field is a two-dimensional array, with each element being an array representing one data record.

Example of querying data from database:
```json
{
    "columns":["TS","HIGH","OPEN","LOW","CLOSE","VOLUME"],
    "values":[
        [1518970320000,100,99.1,90,100,12345.6],
        [1518960320000,100,99.1,90,100,12345.6]
    ]
}
```

See also: `DBExec`, `Dial`

#### Dial-return

The connection object returned by `Dial`. WebSocket (```ws```, ```wss```), TCP (```tcp```, ```tls```) and database connections all return this object; database connections also have ```exec()```. When the connection fails, ```Dial()``` returns a null value and logs an error (```Rust``` returns a connection object whose ```Valid()``` is ```false```).

Fields:

- `read(timeout)` (function): Reads one message. ```timeout``` is in milliseconds: without it the call blocks until data arrives; a positive value is the maximum wait, returning a null value on timeout. Two values apply to WebSocket only: ```-1``` does not wait and returns a null value at once if there is no data; ```-2``` does not wait and returns only the newest message, discarding older ones in the buffer.
- `write(data)` (function): Sends data and returns the number of bytes sent; ```0``` when the connection is closed.
- `close()` (function): Closes the connection. A WebSocket connection with automatic reconnection (```reconnect=true``` in the address) is reconnected by the runtime and need not be closed; a closed connection cannot be used again.
- `exec(sql, ...args)` (function): Database connections only: executes an SQL statement; usage and return value as `DBExec` (see `DBExec-return`). In ```JavaScript``` and ```Python``` the values for ```?``` placeholders can follow the SQL statement.
- `fd()` (function): ```JavaScript``` only: returns a handle to the same connection. Pass the handle to another thread (for example as an argument of ```threading.Thread()```) and call ```Dial(handle)``` there to get a connection object for the same connection; works for WebSocket, TCP and database connections. The handle's ```valueOf()``` is the connection number.
- `Valid()` (function): ```Rust``` only: whether the connection was established.

In ```JavaScript``` a database connection object itself can also be passed to a thread created by ```threading.Thread()```, stored in ```threading.Dict()``` or sent to another thread with ```postMessage()```, sharing one connection between threads; the connection is closed automatically when the object is no longer referenced. ```Python``` and ```Rust``` cannot share connections between threads.

The receive buffer of ```read()``` and its behavior for each ```timeout```:

Data received over WebSocket goes into a receive buffer (a queue) and accumulates when ```read()``` calls are far apart; by default the buffer holds at most 4096 messages or 16 MB (whichever comes first) and drops the oldest data beyond that. The limits can be changed with ```qsize``` and ```qbytes``` in the ```Dial()``` address.

| Situation | No argument | -1 | -2 | 2000 (ms) |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Buffer has data | Returns the oldest data at once | Returns the oldest data at once | Returns the newest data at once, discarding the rest | Returns the oldest data at once |
| Buffer is empty | Blocks until data arrives | Returns a null value at once | Returns a null value at once | Waits at most 2000 ms; null value if no data |
| Connection closed or reconnecting | Returns an empty string ```""``` | -- | -- | -- |

See also: `Dial`, `DBExec`, `EventLoop`

#### Thread.join-return

This JSON is the data structure returned by the ```join()``` member function of the ```Thread``` object, used to store information related to concurrent threads in ```JavaScript``` language strategies. The ```Thread``` object refers to a thread object created via ```threading.Thread()```.

Fields:

- `id` (number): Thread ID.
- `terminated` (bool): Whether the thread was forcibly terminated.
- `elapsed` (number): Thread execution time (nanoseconds).
- `error` (string): Error message when the thread fails (throws an exception); ```null``` when there is no error.
- `ret` (any): Return value of the thread function, which can be of any type; ```undefined``` when the thread function returns nothing.

```join(timeout)``` returns ```undefined``` (not ```null```) when the thread has not finished within the timeout; you can call ```join()``` again later to keep waiting. The following code tests the timeout mechanism of the ```join()``` function of the ```Thread``` object and prints the return value of the ```join()``` function.
```javascript
function testFunc() {
    for (var i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
        Log(i)
        Sleep(300)
    }
}

function main() {
    var t1 = threading.Thread(testFunc)
    Log(t1.join(1000))  // undefined
    Log(t1.join())      // {"id":1,"terminated":false,"elapsed":1506864000,"error":null}
}
```

See also: `join`

## Built-in Variables and Constants

Built-in variables and constants: the exchange objects `exchange` and `exchanges`, and the constant groups for order status, order side, conditional order type, position direction, open/close, K-line period and log type.

Each constant group's page has a table of constants, values and meanings; constants are numbers and can be compared directly with structure fields, for example ```order.Status == ORDER_STATE_CLOSED```.

### EXCHANGE

Exchange objects: `exchange` is the first exchange object added in the robot or backtest configuration, and `exchanges` is the array of all exchange objects in the order they were added, so ```exchanges[0]``` is ```exchange```.

Market, trading, account and futures functions are member functions of an exchange object, for example ```exchange.GetTicker()``` and ```exchanges[1].GetAccount()```, and act only on the account bound to that object.

#### exchange

exchange is an exchange object, and it is also the first exchange object added in the strategy live trading settings and backtesting settings. All interactions with the exchange are implemented through the member functions of this object.

Print the name and label of the first exchange object.

```javascript
function main() {
    Log("First exchange object name:", exchange.GetName(), ", Label:", exchange.GetLabel())
}
```

```python
def main():
    Log("First exchange object name:", exchange.GetName(), ", Label:", exchange.GetLabel())
```

```rust
fn main() {
    Log!("First exchange object name:", exchange.GetName(), ", Label:", exchange.GetLabel());
}
```

See also: `exchanges`, `exchange.GetName`, `exchange.GetLabel`

#### exchanges

exchanges is an array of exchange objects that contains all the exchange objects added in the strategy's live trading settings or backtesting settings, where exchanges[0] is `exchange`.

The exchange objects added in the strategy's live trading settings or backtesting settings correspond to exchanges[0], exchanges[1], exchanges[2], …… exchanges[n] in the order they were added.

Iterate over all exchange objects and print each name and label.

```javascript
function main() {
    for(var i = 0; i < exchanges.length; i++) {
        Log("Exchange index:", i, "Name:", exchanges[i].GetName(), "Label:",
            exchanges[i].GetLabel())
    }
}
```

```python
def main():
    for i in range(len(exchanges)):
        Log("Exchange index:", i, "Name:", exchanges[i].GetName(), "Label:",
            exchanges[i].GetLabel())
```

```rust
fn main() {
    for i in 0..exchanges.len() {
        Log!("Exchange index:", i, "Name:", exchanges[i].GetName(), "Label:",
            exchanges[i].GetLabel());
    }
}
```

See also: `exchange`, `exchange.GetName`, `exchange.GetLabel`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `ORDER_STATE_PENDING` | ```0``` | The order is pending (open, possibly partially filled) |

| `ORDER_STATE_UNKNOWN` | ```3``` | The order status is unknown (any other status) |

The order is pending (open, possibly partially filled); the value is ```0```. Used in the ```Status``` field of the `Order` structure.

#### ORDER_STATE_CLOSED

The order is completed (fully filled); the value is ```1```. Used in the ```Status``` field of the `Order` structure.

#### ORDER_STATE_CANCELED

The order is canceled; the value is ```2```. Used in the ```Status``` field of the `Order` structure.

### ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE

Conditional order type constants: the values of the ```ConditionType``` field of the `Condition` structure, used when creating, modifying and querying conditional orders. Ordinary orders have no condition (in Rust, ```Condition.ConditionType``` of an ```Order``` is ```-1```).

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_OCO` | ```0``` | An OCO order (One-Cancels-the-Other): take-profit and stop-loss conditions are set together, and when one triggers the other is canceled automatically |
| `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_TP` | ```1``` | A take-profit order: an order is placed when the price reaches the take-profit trigger price |
| `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_SL` | ```2``` | A stop-loss order: an order is placed when the price reaches the stop-loss trigger price, to limit losses |
| `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_GENERIC` | ```3``` | A generic conditional order: its behavior depends on the exchange, and it only appears in query results |

#### ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_OCO

An OCO order (One-Cancels-the-Other): take-profit and stop-loss conditions are set together, and when one triggers the other is canceled automatically; the value is ```0```. Used in the ```ConditionType``` field of the `Condition` structure.

See also: `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE`, `Condition`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`

#### ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_TP

A take-profit order: an order is placed when the price reaches the take-profit trigger price; the value is ```1```. Used in the ```ConditionType``` field of the `Condition` structure.

See also: `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE`, `Condition`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`

#### ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_SL

A stop-loss order: an order is placed when the price reaches the stop-loss trigger price, to limit losses; the value is ```2```. Used in the ```ConditionType``` field of the `Condition` structure.

See also: `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE`, `Condition`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`

#### ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE_GENERIC

A generic conditional order: its behavior depends on the exchange, and it only appears in query results; the value is ```3```. Used in the ```ConditionType``` field of the `Condition` structure.

The GENERIC type only appears in query results; `exchange.CreateConditionOrder` and `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder` do not accept it, and passing it returns a null value and logs an error.

See also: `ORDER_CONDITION_TYPE`, `Condition`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`

## Conventions

Conventions shared by the pages of this manual: how instruments are written, query ranges, and what failed or unsupported calls return. Function pages describe only what is specific to the function; the common ground is collected here.

### Symbols

Functions of exchange objects specify an instrument with the string parameter ```symbol```. The notation is defined by the platform and does not depend on the exchange's own API notation, so this part of the code does not change when you switch exchanges.

#### Omitting symbol

Single-instrument functions (```GetTicker```, ```GetDepth```, ```GetTrades```, ```GetRecords```, ```GetHistoryOrders```, etc.) act on the **current instrument** when ```symbol``` is omitted: the current trading pair is set by `exchange.SetCurrency` (initially the pair configured for the live trading or backtest), and for futures the contract code is set by `exchange.SetContractType`. Multi-instrument queries use a range when ```symbol``` is omitted; see "Query ranges" below.

#### Trading pairs

A spot instrument is written as "BASE_QUOTE" in upper case, separated by an underscore ```_```: ```BTC_USDT``` is BTC quoted in USDT, ```ETH_BTC``` is ETH quoted in BTC.

#### Contracts

On a futures exchange object an instrument is written as "pair.contractCode", separated by ```.```:

| Notation | Meaning |
| - | - |
| ```BTC_USDT.swap``` | BTC USDT-margined perpetual |
| ```BTC_USD.swap``` | BTC coin-margined perpetual |
| ```BTC_USDT.quarter``` | BTC USDT-margined quarterly contract |
| ```BTC_USD.this_week``` | BTC coin-margined weekly contract |

The quote currency tells the margin type: stablecoins such as ```USDT``` and ```USDC``` mean USDT-margined (linear), ```USD``` means coin-margined (inverse). The common contract codes are ```swap``` (perpetual), ```this_week```, ```next_week```, ```quarter``` and ```next_quarter```; which ones an exchange supports is described in `exchange.SetContractType`.

The default contract of a cryptocurrency futures exchange object is the perpetual ```swap```: until ```exchange.SetContractType()``` is called, market and trading functions called without ```symbol``` act on the perpetual contract of the current trading pair.

#### Options

An option is written as "pair.optionCode", where the option code is the exchange's own notation. For example, the ```Futures_Binance``` (Binance Futures) option ```BTC-240108-40000-C``` is written ```BTC_USDT.BTC-240108-40000-C```.

#### Native codes

Commodity futures and stock exchanges (```Futures_CTP``` (CTP commodity futures), ```Futures_Futu``` (Futu), ```Futures_IB``` (Interactive Brokers)) have no "pair.contractCode" split: the instrument is the exchange's native contract code, for example ```rb2501``` on CTP. Futu and Interactive Brokers codes may themselves contain ```.``` (for example ```00700.HK```); the whole string is one instrument and is not split.

#### Query ranges

```GetOrders```, ```GetPositions```, ```GetConditionOrders``` and ```GetFundings``` can query many instruments at once. ```symbol``` may be a specific instrument or a range written as "quote.contractType":

| symbol | Range |
| - | - |
| ```USDT.swap``` | USDT-margined perpetuals |
| ```USDT.futures``` | USDT-margined delivery contracts |
| ```USD.swap``` | Coin-margined perpetuals |
| ```USD.futures``` | Coin-margined delivery contracts |
| ```USDT.option``` | USDT-margined options |
| ```USD.option``` | Coin-margined options |
| ```USD.futures_combo``` | Spread combos (```Futures_Deribit``` inverse combos) |
| ```USD.futures_ff``` | Linear delivery contracts (```Futures_Kraken```, contract codes ending in ```_ff```) |
| ```USD.swap_pf``` | Linear perpetuals (```Futures_Kraken```, contract code ```swap_pf```) |

Use the quote currency the exchange actually uses (for example ```USDC.swap```). A range the exchange API does not support is reported as an error and returns a null value.

##### Default range when ```symbol``` is omitted or an empty string ```""```

- Spot exchange objects: all instruments.
- Cryptocurrency futures exchange objects: "current quote currency + contract type of the current contract". The type is ```futures_combo``` for a combo contract (a contract code containing a comma, such as ```quarter,swap```, or a native Deribit combo code, such as ```BTC-FS-26DEC25_PERP```), ```option``` for an option contract, ```swap_pf``` for ```swap_pf```, ```futures_ff``` for codes ending in ```_ff```, ```swap``` for other codes containing ```swap```, and ```futures``` otherwise; with no contract set it is ```swap```. For example, with the current instrument ```BTC_USDT.swap``` this equals passing ```"USDT.swap"```; with ```BTC_USD.quarter``` it equals ```"USD.futures"```; with ```BTC_USD.quarter,swap``` it equals ```"USD.futures_combo"```.
- Futures exchange objects without a "quote + contract type" split (```Futures_CTP```, ```Futures_Futu```, ```Futures_IB```, ```Futures_Polymarket```): all instruments.
- A few exchanges require an instrument in their query API; on these exchanges ```GetOrders``` and ```GetConditionOrders``` without ```symbol``` query only the current trading pair.

A successful query with no data in the range returns an empty array ```[]```; a failed call returns a null value, see `Failures and null values`. ```GetHistoryOrders``` and ```GetHistoryConditionOrders``` do not take ranges; without ```symbol``` they query the current instrument.

### Failures and null values

#### Failed calls return a null value

When a function of an exchange object, or most global functions, fails (network error, timeout, the exchange rejects the request, a parameter the exchange does not accept, etc.), the strategy **is not stopped**. Instead:

1. an error log entry is written (it can be filtered with `SetErrorFilter`);
2. the error message is kept as the last error and can be read with `GetLastError`;
3. a null value is returned: ```null``` in ```JavaScript```, ```None``` in ```Python```, ```Err``` in ```Rust``` (carrying the error message).

A successful query with no data returns an empty array ```[]``` (for example ```exchange.GetOrders()``` with no open orders), which is different from the null value of a failure. Tell the two apart when checking results, and never treat a null value as "no data" and keep calculating. A few functions return something else on failure; the "Returns" section of each function page is authoritative (for example ```HttpQuery()``` returns an empty string on failure).

#### Unsupported functions

When an exchange or the runtime does not support a function or a query range, the call is treated as a failure: an "unsupported" error is recorded (error log + ```GetLastError()```), a null value is returned and the strategy keeps running. It **never** returns values that look like data, such as ```[]```, ```{}``` or ```0```.

#### Programming errors throw

When the call itself is wrong (for example calling a function without ```symbol``` before any trading pair is set, or passing a parameter that cannot be parsed), ```JavaScript``` and ```Python``` throw an exception, which stops the strategy if it is not caught; ```Rust``` returns ```Err```. Such errors need a code change; retrying does not help.

#### Pattern

Check for the null value before using a result; wrap calls that should be retried automatically with `_C`.

Distinguish a failed call (null value) from a successful query with no data (empty array).

```javascript
function main() {
    var ticker = exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT")
    if (ticker === null) {
        // the call failed: the error is already logged and GetLastError() returns the reason
        Log("GetTicker failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    }
    var orders = exchange.GetOrders("BTC_USDT")
    if (orders === null) {
        Log("GetOrders failed:", GetLastError())
    } else if (orders.length === 0) {
        Log("no open orders")
    } else {
        Log("open orders:", orders.length)
    }
}
```

```python
def main():
    ticker = exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT")
    if ticker is None:
        # the call failed: the error is already logged and GetLastError() returns the reason
        Log("GetTicker failed:", GetLastError())
        return
    orders = exchange.GetOrders("BTC_USDT")
    if orders is None:
        Log("GetOrders failed:", GetLastError())
    elif len(orders) == 0:
        Log("no open orders")
    else:
        Log("open orders:", len(orders))
```

```rust
fn main() {
    let ticker = match exchange.GetTicker("BTC_USDT") {
        Ok(t) => t,
        Err(e) => {
            // the call failed: Err carries the error message
            Log!("GetTicker failed:", e);
            return;
        }
    };
    Log!("last:", ticker.Last);
    match exchange.GetOrders("BTC_USDT") {
        Ok(orders) if orders.is_empty() => Log!("no open orders"),
        Ok(orders) => Log!("open orders:", orders.len()),
        Err(e) => Log!("GetOrders failed:", e),
    }
}
```

## Exchanges

This chapter is the reference for the exchange objects: one page per brand, with the spot and futures exchange objects of a brand on the same page. Each page gives the names (the ```exchange.GetName()``` value and aliases), the configuration fields, trading pairs and contract codes, exchange-specific IO commands, unsupported and fallback functions, margin, account and simulation, options and notes. Function pages describe the common semantics; differences between exchanges are documented here. Function support and trading-mode commands of all exchanges are summarized in `Capability Matrix`.

### Names

An exchange object is named by the value of ```exchange.GetName()```; click a name for its exchange page.

| ```exchange.GetName()``` | Brand | Type | Aliases |
| - | - | - | - |
| `AscendEx` | AscendEx | Spot | AscendEX, BitMax |
| `Backpack` | Backpack | Spot | Backpack Exchange |
| `Futures_Backpack` | Backpack | Futures | — |
| `BigONE` | BigONE | Spot | — |
| `Binance` | Binance | Spot | — |
| `Futures_Binance` | Binance | Futures | — |
| `Bitfinex` | Bitfinex | Spot | — |
| `Futures_Bitfinex` | Bitfinex | Futures | Bitfinex Futures |

### Capability Matrix

Support of the standard functions and trading-mode commands per exchange object. ✓ supported; ✗ not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null); Synth: the exchange's API does not fully provide the function (no such endpoint, or some K-line periods missing, etc.) and the docker fills the gap, see the exchange page; — not applicable (spot exchange objects have no futures functions).

### Centralized Exchanges

Centralized crypto exchanges, one page per brand; the spot and futures exchange objects of a brand share the page.

#### AscendEx

AscendEx spot, with the cash wallet and the margin wallet (switch with ```exchange.IO("trade_margin")```).

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```AscendEx``` (Spot); aliases: AscendEX, BitMax.

| Field | Required |
| - | - |
| Access Key | Yes |
| Secret Key | Yes |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDT```, ```ETH_USDT```

Trading pairs are written ```BASE_QUOTE```, matching the AscendEx native code ```BTC/USDT```.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| ```"trade_margin"``` | Switch to the margin wallet. Account, order placement, cancellation, order queries, open and historical orders and ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` then use the margin wallet endpoints; ```exchange.GetTickers()``` fails on the margin wallet. |
| ```"trade_normal"``` | Switch back to the cash wallet (the default). |

For the common commands ```api```, ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.CancelConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`, `exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 12h, 1d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

##### Notes

- The exchange has ceased operation.
- The amount of a spot market buy order is in the base currency, not a quote-currency amount.

#### Backpack

```Backpack``` (Spot): Spot trading on Backpack Exchange (mainly USDC-quoted), including the tokenized stocks listed on the exchange. Perpetual contracts are served by the Futures_Backpack exchange object.

```Futures_Backpack``` (Futures): Backpack Exchange USDC perpetual contracts, including perpetuals on tokenized stocks. Spot is served by the Backpack exchange object.

##### Names and Configuration

| ```exchange.GetName()``` | Type | Aliases |
| - | - | - |
| ```Backpack``` | Spot | Backpack Exchange |
| ```Futures_Backpack``` | Futures | — |

| Field | Required |
| - | - |
| Access Key | Yes |
| Secret Key | Yes |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

###### ```Backpack``` (Spot)

Pair examples: ```SOL_USDC```, ```BTC_USDC```, ```SPCX-US_USDC```

Trading pairs are written as ```SOL_USDC```. Tokenized stocks whose exchange name contains ```.``` (such as ```SPCX.US```) are written with ```-``` in pairs and asset names: ```SPCX-US_USDC```.

###### ```Futures_Backpack``` (Futures)

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDC```, ```ETH_USDC```

Backpack perpetuals are quoted in USDC; trading pairs are written as ```ETH_USDC``` (USDC is assumed when the quote currency is omitted). Tokenized stocks whose exchange name contains ```.``` (such as ```MU.US```) are written with ```-``` in pairs and asset names: ```MU-US_USDC```.

| Contract code | Description |
| - | - |
| ```swap``` | Perpetual contract (exchange code ```ETH_USDC_PERP```); the full symbol looks like ```ETH_USDC.swap```. |

Backpack lists perpetual contracts only; any other contract code is rejected.

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

###### ```Backpack``` (Spot)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```"selfTradePreventionMode"``` | string | Self-trade prevention for subsequent orders and conditional orders; one of ```Allow```, ```RejectTaker```, ```RejectMaker```, ```RejectBoth``` (case-sensitive). | Null on success; an error for any other value. |

For the common commands ```api```, ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

###### ```Futures_Backpack``` (Futures)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```"selfTradePreventionMode"``` | string | Self-trade prevention for subsequent orders and conditional orders; one of ```Allow```, ```RejectTaker```, ```RejectMaker```, ```RejectBoth``` (case-sensitive). | The value set on success; an error for any other value. |

For the common commands ```api```, ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### ```Futures_Backpack``` (Futures)

Margin mode: Backpack uses a unified collateral account with cross margin only and no cross/isolated switch. ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` changes the account-level leverage limit (```leverageLimit```), which applies to all contracts; the call also turns on the account's auto-borrow settings (```autoBorrowSettlements```, ```autoLend```, ```autoRepayBorrows```).

Position mode: One-way (net) positions only, no hedge mode. Closing orders (```closebuy```, ```closesell```) are placed as reduce-only (```reduceOnly```). ```MarginLevel``` in ```exchange.GetPositions()``` is the reciprocal of the initial margin fraction.

Account: ```exchange.GetAccount()``` reads the collateral account: ```Balance``` is the available net equity, ```FrozenBalance``` the locked net equity and ```Equity``` the net equity; each collateral currency is listed in ```exchange.GetAssets()```.

##### Notes

###### All exchange objects

- The client order ID ```clientId``` must be an integer from 0 to 4294967295; any other value fails and the order is not sent.
- The batch data of ```exchange.GetTickers()``` has no order book, so ```Buy``` and ```Sell``` are the last trade price; use ```exchange.GetTicker()``` for the real best bid and ask.
- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO. Backpack trigger orders do not distinguish take-profit from stop-loss, so the type is inferred on query from the trigger price relative to the current last price. With an order price of 0 the order executes at market once triggered. Modifying a conditional order is not supported; cancel and recreate it instead.
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` query one symbol at a time and do not support ```since``` (the exchange's order history endpoint has no time range); a ```since``` greater than 0 or an empty symbol is rejected.

###### ```Backpack``` (Spot)

- The amount of a market buy order is the quote currency to spend (placed with Backpack's ```quoteQuantity```); a market sell order uses the base currency amount. Such market buy orders have no order price in queries, so ```Price``` is 0.
- ```exchange.GetAccount()``` and ```exchange.GetAssets()``` count available and frozen amounts only, not staked amounts.

###### ```Futures_Backpack``` (Futures)

- The amount of a market order is the contract quantity (in the base currency) for both buys and sells.
- Funding intervals differ between contracts; ```exchange.GetFundings()``` reports each one from the exchange's contract information.

#### BigONE

BigONE spot.

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```BigONE``` (Spot).

| Field | Required |
| - | - |
| Access Key | Yes |
| Secret Key | Yes |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDT```, ```ETH_BTC```

Trading pairs are written ```BASE_QUOTE```, matching the BigONE native code ```BTC-USDT```.

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 3h, 4h, 6h, 12h, 1d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

##### Notes

- Market orders are not supported, only limit orders; FOK is not supported (a ```tif``` of ```"fok"``` fails), while IOC and maker-only (```postOnly```) are supported.
- The open-order and open-conditional-order endpoints require a trading pair: without the ```symbol``` argument, ```exchange.GetOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetConditionOrders()``` query the current trading pair only.
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` do not support the ```since``` argument (the exchange API has no time-range parameter) and fail when it is given; without it they return the most recent orders.
- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss (without an order price they execute at market once triggered), not OCO.

#### Binance

```Binance``` (Spot): Binance spot, plus Binance margin accounts (isolated and cross) and cross margin trading under a unified (portfolio margin) account.

```Futures_Binance``` (Futures): Binance USDⓈ-M (USDT- and USDC-margined) and COIN-M perpetual and delivery contracts, plus Binance European options (USDT-settled).

##### Names and Configuration

| ```exchange.GetName()``` | Type |
| - | - |
| ```Binance``` | Spot |
| ```Futures_Binance``` | Futures |

| Field | Required | Default |
| - | - | - |
| Access Key | Yes | — |
| Secret Key | Yes | — |
| Simulate | No | Unchecked |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

###### ```Binance``` (Spot)

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDT```, ```ETH_BTC```

Pairs are written as ```BTC_USDT``` without a contract code; symbols with a contract suffix such as ```.swap``` are rejected (use a Futures_Binance exchange object for contracts).

###### ```Futures_Binance``` (Futures)

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDT```, ```BTC_USDC```, ```BTC_USD```

The quote currency selects the contract family: ```BTC_USDT``` and ```BTC_USDC``` are USDⓈ-M contracts, ```BTC_USD``` is COIN-M. Binance trading pairs with Chinese names are supported, for example ```币安人生_USDT.swap```.

| Contract code | Description |
| - | - |
| ```swap``` | Perpetual contract (the default), available as USDⓈ-M and COIN-M. |
| ```quarter``` | Current-quarter delivery contract. Listed for COIN-M; USDⓈ-M only for some coins. |
| ```next_quarter``` | Next-quarter delivery contract, listed like ```quarter```. |

Common contract codes not available: ```this_week```, ```next_week```.

Binance has no weekly contracts; ```this_week``` and ```next_week``` are rejected.

Native contract code examples: ```BTCUSDT_260925```, ```BTCUSD_260925```

Delivery contracts can also be given by their Binance native code (the pair without the underscore, then ```_``` and the delivery date).

##### Exchange-specific IO Commands

###### ```Binance``` (Spot)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```"trade_margin"``` | — | Switch to the isolated margin account; account, order and order-query calls then use the isolated margin API. The demo environment has no margin API and reports an error. | The command name itself (```"trade_margin"```). |
| ```"trade_super_margin"``` | — | Switch to the cross margin account (not available on demo). When the account is a unified account, the unified account's (papi.binance.com) cross margin API is used. | The command name itself (```"trade_super_margin"```). |
| ```"trade_normal"``` | — | Switch back to the normal spot account (the default). | The command name itself (```"trade_normal"```). |
| ```"unified"``` | bool | Unified account (portfolio margin); only takes effect under cross margin (```trade_super_margin```). When not set, it is detected automatically on the first request after switching to cross margin. | Null also on success; check GetLastError() afterwards when needed. |
| ```"selfTradePreventionMode"``` | string | Self-trade prevention for subsequent orders; one of ```EXPIRE_TAKER```, ```EXPIRE_MAKER```, ```EXPIRE_BOTH```, ```NONE```. | Null also on success; check GetLastError() afterwards when needed. |

For the common commands ```api```, ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

###### ```Futures_Binance``` (Futures)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```"cross"``` | bool[, symbol] | Cross (true) / isolated (false) margin. | Null also on success; check GetLastError() afterwards when needed. |
| ```"dual"``` | bool[, symbol] | Hedge (true) / one-way (false) position mode, set separately for USDⓈ-M and COIN-M. | Null also on success; check GetLastError() afterwards when needed. |
| ```"unified"``` | bool[, symbol] | Unified account (portfolio margin), using papi.binance.com after switching; detected automatically on the first private request when not set. Fails while the current contract is an option. | — |
| ```"selfTradePreventionMode"``` | string | Self-trade prevention for subsequent orders; one of ```EXPIRE_TAKER```, ```EXPIRE_MAKER```, ```EXPIRE_BOTH```, ```NONE```. | — |
| ```"coinmBase"``` | [string] | Query or switch the COIN-M API base address (the ```"base"``` command covers USDⓈ-M only). | The address before the change. |
| ```"eapiBase"``` | [string] | Query or switch the options API base address. | The address before the change. |

For the common commands ```api```, ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Function Support

###### ```Binance``` (Spot)

No unsupported standard functions.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1s, 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

###### ```Futures_Binance``` (Futures)

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### ```Binance``` (Spot)

Account: The default is the normal spot account; ```exchange.IO("trade_margin")``` and ```exchange.IO("trade_super_margin")``` switch to the isolated and cross margin accounts, after which all account and order calls use the corresponding margin API until ```exchange.IO("trade_normal")``` switches back. Under isolated margin, ```exchange.GetAssets()``` sums each coin's balance across the isolated pairs.

Simulation: The Simulate box uses the Binance demo environment (```demo-api.binance.com```). The demo environment has no margin API; only normal spot can be traded.

###### ```Futures_Binance``` (Futures)

Margin mode: Switch cross/isolated margin per contract with ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)```; set leverage with ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()```. A unified account is always cross margin; switching to isolated fails.

Position mode: Switch hedge/one-way mode with ```exchange.IO("dual", bool)```; USDⓈ-M and COIN-M are independent. Orders carry position parameters matching the account's actual mode, or an explicit ```positionSide``` in the order's extra parameters.

Account: A unified (portfolio margin) account is detected on the first private request, or set with ```exchange.IO("unified", bool)```. Under a unified account the ```Balance``` of ```exchange.GetAccount()``` is all assets converted to USD; divide it by an asset's index price and then by its collateral ratio to get the amount in that asset.

Simulation: The Simulate box uses the Binance demo environment (```demo-fapi```, ```demo-dapi```). The demo environment has no options API, so option calls fail in simulation (an options base address can be set explicitly with ```exchange.IO("eapiBase", url)```).

##### Options

###### ```Futures_Binance``` (Futures)

Binance European options (USDT-settled) are supported; options trading must be enabled on the account, and the exchange may require a separate seller qualification. Limitations:

- Only limit orders; market orders, conditional orders and order amendment (```exchange.ModifyOrder()```) are not supported.
- ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` and ```exchange.GetFundings()``` are not supported, and option contracts cannot switch margin mode.
- ```exchange.IO("unified", true)``` fails while the current contract is an option; if the account itself is a unified account, options are still traded through the options API.
- ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` does not list option contracts; get option codes from the Binance API or website.

Option code examples: ```BTC-260925-145000-C```, ```XRP-240112-0.5-C```

Option codes are Binance native codes: underlying-expiry (YYMMDD)-strike-C/P, C for a call and P for a put. Binance options settle in USDT; set the trading pair to ```BTC_USDT```, the full symbol looks like ```BTC_USDT.BTC-260925-145000-C```.

##### Notes

###### ```Binance``` (Spot)

- ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` and ```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()``` use Binance's cancel-replace endpoint (```cancelReplace```; no new order is placed if the cancellation fails) and return the new order's ID, which should be used from then on; only the normal spot account is supported, margin accounts report an error.
- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO; create a take-profit order and a stop-loss order separately when needed.

###### ```Futures_Binance``` (Futures)

- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO (Binance futures have no OCO endpoint); modifying a conditional order is not supported, cancel and recreate it instead.

For the common commands ```api```, ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Function Support

No unsupported standard functions.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 3h, 6h, 12h, 1d, 1w, 14d, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### ```Futures_Bitfinex``` (Futures)

Account: Futures margin sits on the ```F0```-suffixed currencies (such as ```USTF0```) of the Bitfinex margin wallet; `exchange.GetAccount` returns the currencies without the suffix (```USTF0``` shows as ```USDT```). Bitfinex has no set-leverage endpoint: ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` only records the leverage per contract locally and sends it with each order (10x when not set).

##### Notes

###### All exchange objects

- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO.
- An order ```clientId``` must be a positive integer (Bitfinex's ```cid```); other values report an error. Limit orders support ```tif``` IOC, FOK and maker-only (```postOnly```); market orders do not support FOK or maker-only, and conditional orders do not support IOC or FOK; passing them reports an error.

###### ```Bitfinex``` (Spot)

- The amount of a spot market buy order is in the base currency, not a quote-currency amount.
- Bitfinex prices have 5 significant digits and no fixed tick size; the ```TickSize``` and ```PricePrecision``` returned by `exchange.GetMarkets` are derived from the current last price and change when the price moves to another order of magnitude.

###### ```Futures_Bitfinex``` (Futures)

- Order amounts are in coins, not numbers of contracts.
- Bitfinex prices have 5 significant digits; the ```TickSize``` and ```PricePrecision``` returned by `exchange.GetMarkets` are derived from the current last price.

#### bitFlyer

bitFlyer (Japan) spot. Only spot pairs are served, not bitFlyer's FX and futures products.

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```BitFlyer``` (Spot).

| Field | Required |
| - | - |
| Access Key | Yes |
| Secret Key | Yes |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_JPY```, ```ETH_JPY```

Trading pairs are written ```BASE_QUOTE```, the same form as the bitFlyer native ```product_code```.

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`, `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: The exchange has no K-line endpoint; bars are synthesized by the docker from trades. The first call covers only the few bars spanned by recent trades, and more accumulate with later calls.

##### Notes

- The amount of a spot market buy order is in the base currency, not a quote-currency amount (orders are placed by bitFlyer ```size```).
- Maker-only (```postOnly```) orders are not supported.
- The open-order and open-conditional-order endpoints require a trading pair: without the ```symbol``` argument, ```exchange.GetOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetConditionOrders()``` query the current trading pair only.
- ```exchange.GetHistoryOrders()``` and ```exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders()``` do not support the ```since``` argument (the exchange only pages by order id) and fail when it is given; without it they return the most recent orders.
- Conditional orders use bitFlyer parent orders (SIMPLE) and support take-profit and stop-loss (without an order price they execute at market once triggered), not OCO.
- ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` gives no price/amount precision or order-size limits (the exchange API does not provide them); those fields are 0.

The quote currency selects the contract family: ```BTC_USDT``` and ```BTC_USDC``` are USDT- and USDC-settled contracts (the USDC perpetual is Bitget's ```BTCPERP```), ```BTC_USD``` is coin-margined. | ```"cross"``` | bool[, symbol] | Cross (true, crossed) / isolated (false) margin; sends a switch request to the exchange. A unified account (v3) cannot switch and is always cross margin; the call fails. | Null also on success; check GetLastError() afterwards when needed. |

##### Function Support

###### All exchange objects

No unsupported standard functions.

###### ```Bitget``` (Spot)

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 6h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker. 3m is available only with the unified account (v3).

###### ```Futures_Bitget``` (Futures)

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 6h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker. Coin-margined delivery contracts on a unified account (v3) have no 3d period.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### All exchange objects

Account: The "Version" option selects the account type: v3 for a unified account (private API under ```/api/v3```), v2 for a classic account (under ```/api/v2```). A unified account calling the classic API is rejected by the exchange (40085); choose the version matching the account.

###### ```Bitget``` (Spot)

Simulation: Switch to Bitget demo trading with ```exchange.IO("simulate", true)```; it needs a demo API key.

###### ```Futures_Bitget``` (Futures)

Margin mode: On a classic account (v2) switch cross/isolated margin per contract with ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)```; a unified account (v3) is always cross margin. Set leverage with ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()```.

Position mode: Orders carry open/close parameters matching the account's actual position mode; switch it with ```exchange.IO("dual", bool)```.

Simulation: Switch to Bitget demo trading with ```exchange.IO("simulate", true)```; it needs a demo API key, and pairs are written as ```SBTC_SUSDT``` etc. The unified account (v3) API does not support demo instruments; choose v2 for demo trading.

##### Notes

###### ```Bitget``` (Spot)

- A unified account (v3) has no spot conditional-order API, so conditional-order functions (```exchange.CreateConditionOrder()```, ```exchange.GetConditionOrders()```, etc.) report an error and return null; a classic account (v2) supports take-profit and stop-loss conditional orders (not OCO) and ```exchange.ModifyConditionOrder()```.
- ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` amends in place on a unified account; on a classic account it uses the cancel-replace endpoint (```cancel-replace-order```) and returns the new order's ID.

###### ```Futures_Bitget``` (Futures)

- ```exchange.GetFundings()``` has no batch query; pass a specific perpetual contract, for example ```exchange.GetFundings("ETH_USDT.swap")```.
- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO; create a take-profit order and a stop-loss order separately when needed.
- On a classic account (v2), ```exchange.ModifyOrder()``` has the exchange cancel the old order and place a new one, so the order ID changes and the new ID is returned; a unified account (v3) amends in place.

#### Bybit

```Bybit``` (Spot): Bybit spot, plus spot margin (borrowing on order). Both unified trading accounts (UTA) and classic accounts are supported, using the Bybit V5 API.

```Futures_Bybit``` (Futures): Bybit USDT and USDC perpetual and delivery contracts (linear), coin-margined perpetual and delivery contracts (inverse), and USDT-settled options. Both unified trading accounts (UTA) and classic accounts are supported, using the Bybit V5 API.

##### Names and Configuration

| ```exchange.GetName()``` | Type |
| - | - |
| ```Bybit``` | Spot |
| ```Futures_Bybit``` | Futures |

| Field | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| Access Key | Yes | — | — |
| Secret Key | Yes | — | — |
| Version | Yes | ```v5``` | Kept for compatibility; the connector always uses the Bybit V5 API, whichever version is selected. Options: ```v3```, ```v5``` |
| Simulate | No | Unchecked | — |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

###### ```Bybit``` (Spot)

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDT```, ```ETH_BTC```

Pairs are written as ```BTC_USDT``` without a contract code; use a Futures_Bybit exchange object for contracts.

###### ```Futures_Bybit``` (Futures)

Pair examples: ```BTC_USDT```, ```BTC_USDC```, ```BTC_USD```

The quote currency selects the contract family: ```BTC_USDT``` and ```BTC_USDC``` are linear contracts, ```BTC_USD``` is inverse (coin-margined). The USDC perpetual is Bybit's ```BTCPERP```.

| Contract code | Description |
| - | - |
| ```swap``` | Perpetual contract (the default). |
| ```delivery``` | The nearest-expiry delivery contract. |
| ```this_week``` | Current-week delivery contract. |
| ```next_week``` | Next-week delivery contract. |
| ```third_week``` | Third-week delivery contract. |
| ```month``` | Monthly delivery contract. |
| ```next_month``` | Next-month delivery contract. |
| ```quarter``` | Quarterly delivery contract. |
| ```next_quarter``` | Next-quarter delivery contract. |
| ```third_quarter``` | Third-quarter delivery contract. |

Delivery contracts are picked from the expiries actually listed in the Bybit instrument list: the week tiers map to contracts expiring in each of the next three seven-day windows, month tiers take month-end expiries, and quarter tiers take month-end expiries in March, June, September or December. A tier the exchange has not listed is rejected.

Native contract code examples: ```BTCUSDU26```, ```ETHUSDT-04APR25```

Delivery contracts can also be given by their Bybit native code. Some Bybit delivery contracts have no clear cycle and are used by their native code, for example pair ```ETH_USDT``` with contract code ```ETHUSDT-04APR25```.

| ```"trade_normal"``` | — | Switch back to normal spot (the default). | The command name itself (```"trade_normal"```). |

###### ```Futures_Bybit``` (Futures)

| Command | Arguments | Description | Returns |
| - | - | - | - |
| ```"cross"``` | bool[, symbol] | Cross (true) / isolated (false) margin; sends a switch request to the exchange. Switching to isolated also sets buy and sell leverage (the last ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` value, or 10x if never set). Not available for options. | Null also on success; check GetLastError() afterwards when needed. |
| ```"dual"``` | bool[, symbol] | Hedge (true) / one-way (false) position mode; sends a switch request to the exchange. Not available for options. | Null also on success; check GetLastError() afterwards when needed. |
| ```"accountType"``` | string | Set the account type: ```UNIFIED``` (unified trading account), ```CONTRACT``` (the contract wallet of a classic account); ```auto``` restores auto-detection (the default). | The account type set (```"auto"``` for auto-detection). |

For the common commands ```api```, ```base``` and ```currency``` see `exchange.IO`.

##### Function Support

###### All exchange objects

No unsupported standard functions.

###### ```Bybit``` (Spot)

Served through a fallback:

###### ```Futures_Bybit``` (Futures)

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: Native periods are 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 12h, 1d, 1w, 1M; other periods are synthesized by the docker. Options have no K-line endpoint; their bars are synthesized by the docker from trades.

##### Margin, Account and Simulation

###### All exchange objects

Simulation: The Simulate box uses Bybit Demo Trading (```api-demo.bybit.com```); the API key must be created on the Bybit main site after switching to Demo Trading mode. It is not the same environment as testnet.

###### ```Bybit``` (Spot)

Account: Spot assets of unified trading accounts and classic accounts live in different wallets; the connector queries the account type on the first private request (or set it with ```exchange.IO("accountType", ...)```). Spot margin is enabled with ```exchange.IO("trade_margin")```, after which orders borrow when placed.

###### ```Futures_Bybit``` (Futures)

Margin mode: Switch cross/isolated margin per contract with ```exchange.IO("cross", bool)```; set leverage (the same for buy and sell) with ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()```.

Position mode: The contract's position mode is queried automatically before orders, and ```positionIdx``` is added in hedge mode; ```positionIdx``` can also be passed explicitly in the order's extra parameters, or the mode switched with ```exchange.IO("dual", bool)```.

Account: The account type is detected on the first private request. Under unified trading account 1.0, linear assets are in the unified wallet and inverse assets in the contract wallet; ```exchange.GetAssets()``` queries both.

##### Options

###### ```Futures_Bybit``` (Futures)

Bybit USDT-settled options are supported (Bybit currently lists USDT-settled options only).

- The result of ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` includes option contracts.
- Conditional orders and ```exchange.SetMarginLevel()``` are not supported, and ```cross``` and ```dual``` cannot switch the margin or position mode.

Option code examples: ```ETH-25JUN27-2800-C-USDT```

Option codes are Bybit native codes: underlying-expiry-strike-C/P-settlement coin. Bybit options settle in USDT; set the pair to ```ETH_USDT```, the full symbol looks like ```ETH_USDT.ETH-25JUN27-2800-C-USDT```; the pair's quote currency must match the settlement coin.

##### Notes

###### All exchange objects

- Conditional orders support take-profit and stop-loss only, not OCO; create a take-profit order and a stop-loss order separately when needed.

###### ```Futures_Bybit``` (Futures)

- The result of ```exchange.GetMarkets()``` includes pre-launch (PreLaunch) contracts.

#### Coincheck

Coincheck (Japan) spot.

##### Names and Configuration

```exchange.GetName()```: ```Coincheck``` (Spot).

| Field | Required |
| - | - |
| Access Key | Yes |
| Secret Key | Yes |

##### Trading Pairs and Contract Codes

Pair examples: ```BTC_JPY```, ```ETH_JPY```

Trading pairs are written ```BASE_QUOTE```, matching the Coincheck native code ```btc_jpy```; the tradable pairs are whatever the exchange lists.

##### Function Support

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.GetTickers`, `exchange.GetMarkets`, `exchange.GetHistoryOrders`, `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders`.

Served through a fallback:

- `exchange.GetRecords`: The exchange has no K-line endpoint; bars are synthesized by the docker from trades. The first call covers only the few bars spanned by recent trades, and more accumulate with later calls.
- `exchange.GetOrder`: The exchange has no single-order query interface, so the order is looked up among the current open orders; the exchange provides no historical order query, so filled or canceled orders cannot be found (null is returned).

##### Notes

- Maker-only (```postOnly```, limit orders only) orders are supported; the ```tif``` (IOC, FOK) option is not and reports an error.
- Conditional orders use the ```stop_loss_rate``` (trigger price) of the Coincheck order endpoint and support take-profit and stop-loss (without an order price they execute at market once triggered), not OCO; conditional orders are canceled through the same endpoint as normal orders.
- When ```exchange.GetConditionOrders()``` is called without the ```symbol``` argument, take-profit and stop-loss cannot be told apart from the current price, and the conditional orders are returned with the generic condition type.

Coinone (Korea) spot, the KRW market.

```exchange.GetName()```: ```Coinone``` (Spot).

| Field | Required |
| - | - |

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders`.

Served through a fallback:

- ```exchange.GetTickers()``` returns the tickers of all KRW-market pairs.
- Maker-only (```postOnly```, limit orders only) orders are supported; the ```tif``` (IOC, FOK) option is not and reports an error.
- Conditional orders use Coinone ```STOP_LIMIT``` orders and support take-profit and stop-loss; an order price after triggering is required (executing at market once triggered is not supported), and OCO is not supported; conditional orders are canceled through the same endpoint as normal orders.
- The open orders returned by ```exchange.GetOrders()``` include untriggered conditional orders (```STOP_LIMIT```).
- The exchange's completed orders carry no order type, so historical conditional orders cannot be queried.

##### Function Support

###### ```Coinw``` (Spot)

Not supported (the call fails with an error and returns null): `exchange.ModifyOrder`, `exchange.CreateConditionOrder`, `exchange.ModifyConditionOrder`, `exchange.CancelConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrder`, `exchange.GetConditionOrders`, `exchange.GetHistoryConditionOrders`.
